{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_quenelles_second_2}Lady Mathilde is atypical for most damsels, in that instead of the ‘typical’ enigmatic wandering, she remains at the side of Ser Leon. There is much speculation as to why this is, whether they are some kind of holy lovers, that she is on a troth from the Lady herself, or that perhaps they are long lost siblings. Regardless as a Damsel of the Lady, her mere presence demands the respect of all Bretonnians. Woe be upon any who insult her, even accidentally, for the presence of Ser Leon will not allow any besmirchment to go unchecked.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_factionleader}Louen took the Questing when he was still a young prince. For years he travelled across Bretonnia and lands beyond, purging evil wherever it could be found. He met many Mythical Characters and killed many daemons and dragons. The grand court of Couronne cared not for hollow boasts however, he knew that to prove his victories he needed to complete his quest. For five long years Louen travelled, until news had reached him that an army of undead was headed towards the northernmost villages of Couronne. Seeking aid, Louen had returned home. His father was disgusted that he returned home with nothing more than a beggar's plea. Louen and sixteen knights rode alongside him to meet the undead army. They killed many undead, but were eventually overwhelmed. Louen was stabbed with a rusty blade and fell into a nearby river. He awoke not on the bottom of a river but in a beautiful courtroom, inhabited by many strange and wonderful creatures. Watching over them was a stunning female figure. Louen recognised her at once and knelt, for he was in the presence of the lady of the lake. She exclaimed that dark times will soon befall bretonnia and that a strong king is needed to guide the kingdom through it. Louen would be that king. He supped the holy waters from her cupped hands. and on a sudden impulse even received a kiss from the lady. It was then that he was dubbed Louen Leoncouer, the heart of the lion. Reinvigorated, Louen rode out of the river with a host of spectral knights at his back. They charged through the thick lines of undead and Louen managed to kill the necromancer with a swift slash of his shield. The necromancer lay dead, his undead army crumbled, and Louen returned home.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_first_2}A stalwart knight who guards the north-eastern shoreline. Tall and broad-shouldered, with weathered features and an unkempt beard. Philippe keeps a constant vigil against the growing threat of marauders. With determination and unwavering resolve, tempered by a deep sense of duty, he will protect his people.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_first_3}Renowned for his extravagant way of sword fighting, preferring precise thrusts over broad strikes in combat. Tall and lean, with piercing blue eyes and a stern face, Jehan is an imposing figure on the battlefield. His armour, adorned with the sigil of Couronne, shines in the sunlight as he moves gracefully, always ready for a swift strike.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_first_4}A celebrated knight of Bretonnia, known throughout the realm for his skill at the jousting tournaments. With a head full of golden hair and his big bulky features, atop his armoured steed, Gillet is a foe to be reckoned with. It is jokingly said that Gillet could stop a charging imperial steam tank.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_first_5}A master tactician, Gerard keeps the northern shores secure against marauding northmen. Most northmen usually make landfall at the northernmost shores of Couronne, for there is no village there to protect and thus less opposition, they could not be more wrong. Their presence is well known long before they make landfall and the size of the raid usually determines the course of action Gerard takes. Small to medium raids are usually allowed to make landfall, only to be crushed by cavalry as they go south, big raids usually depend more on the fortress that keeps watch over the north, keeping the enemy in place as they are slowly grinded down.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_first_6}The bane of beastmen and greenskins, Southern Couronne sees frequent attacks from wandering beastmen in the south and raiding orcs from the east. They have yet to cross the river Sannez, for Michel la Montagne stands ready to meet them. The lack of tactics and skill from his bestial adversaries has made Michel quite adept at dispatching these would-be invaders, running them through with lance and blade with ease, his long black hair flowing gracefully in the heat of combat.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_first_7}Self proclaimed lord of the Marsh, Adalbert is desperate to join King Louen's inner circle. He aims to perform acts so glorious that the King will have little choice but to accept him. Adalbert is looking for bands of adventurers, pressing for military raids against the Wasteland. If he could capture Marienburg, he is sure that he would be allowed to rule it and join the king’s inner circle.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_first_8}Long ago, Landuin saw his father fall in battle against the necromancer which saw King Louen become a grail knight. Shortly after he also had to fight his father, as he was resurrected to stop Landuin from getting to his new master. Landuin inherited his father’s glittering blue and green eyes and athletic build. He wields the eagle-headed hammer his father used. It is a bitter reminder that there are many evils in the world, evils that need to be purged.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_first_9}Alexandre never liked horses as much as other Couronnians and instead opted for a life of adventuring instead with like minded individuals. Alexandre led a good life, doing the dirty work of lords which knights thought to be unchivalrous, mainly helping with border disputes and levying taxes. It all went wrong however, one day while travelling they stumbled upon a stone troll, the creature waiting for prey on the side of the road. Alixandre and his allies thought it an easy kill but it wasn’t. He stood bloodied and beaten, surrounded by the corpses of his comrades, the drooling troll looming over him ready to beat him to a pulp. Alexandre’s breathing was heavy and ragged. With a final prayer to the lady he swung his blade through the troll's belly. A wave of blood gushed over Alexandre's body, the troll's belly was torn open, and his blade looked as if it was made of pure sunlight. He gave up on adventuring shortly after and took the knight's pledge. Vowing one day to become a grail knight.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_first_10}Orphan and youngest daughter of a Bretonnian nobleman killed in combat. Having received the gift of the Lady, she gained a home at the court of Couronne, and in the heart of Sir Bedivere, whom she accompanies in the search for the grail, as long as King Louen does not need her.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_second_1}The Footman of the Stool is responsible for attending the King whilst he answers the call of nature and emptying the chamber pot afterwards. As a result, this position is always held by a Baron the King trusts implicitly, and as it guarantees personal access to the King several times per day, the Foootman of the Stool is a powerful courtier. Farabus was a brave Grail Knight, until his left leg was crushed by a great Daemon that died under his sword. The King granted him his current position as compensation, and Farabus serves loyally. The Baron fully appreciates the importance of his job, but recently the jokes that always circulate around the court have begun to grate on him. He does not want to leave his job, but he does want to teach the jokers a lesson...

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_second_2}Bertrand was tasked by King Louen himself with assisting the Grail Knights of Tristan de la Tour in destroying the cursed 'Black Grail.' He and his men were stationed in the town of Vingtienne, where they were to await the arrival of the Grail Knights and their foreign allies. While stationed in Vingtienne, the town came under attack by an army of Greenskins. Bertrand's allies arrived just in time, however, and together they were able to defeat the Orcs. Joining up with the coalition army of Empire, Dwarf and Mercenary soldiers, Bertrand and his knights were considered every bit as deadly as the Grudgebringers' most elite cavalry. His Knights belonged to the most numerous of the Bretonnian orders of chivalry. They rode into battle on powerful Bretonnian Warhorses, and were soon known for being highly skilled in combat.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_second_3}Tristan was tasked by King Louen himself with assisting a mighty alliance comprised of troops from the Empire and Kislev, alongside Dwarfs and Wood Elves. Led by the Mercenary force known as the Grudgebringers, this massive army would be sent to the dark city of Mousillon, tasked with destroying one of the Old World's greatest threats, an army of the Undead, led by the resurrected corpses of Tristan's fellow Grail Knights. Tristan and his companions proved to be the deadliest troops in the coalition army. Having sipped from the Grail itself, they were the most powerful of all the Knights of Bretonnia. Their skill in combat was seen as extraordinary, and they fought determinedly. When fighting against the Undead hordes of the Dread King, Tristan and his Grail Knights were the only warriors who showed no fear. Indeed, they were all but immune to such types of psychology.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_third_1}Roland the Marshal is a famed knight of Couronne, who acts as the protector of his dukedom's borderlands. The Marshal or 'Marechal' of Bretonnia is responsible for defending the Marches of Couronne which mark the frontier with Marienburg and the Empire. This is disputed land and much of it is marshy or thickly wooded. It is the scene of many battles with Empire forces and other would-be invaders. The Marshal himself seizes every opportunity to push the frontier a bit further east. Roland leads a retinue of Knights and holds numerous castles, but the region is not yet large enough or stable enough to be made into a dukedom.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_couronne_third_2}As a young knight, d’Artaud gave up the keep and lands that were his due in order to quest for the grail. Now, almost 20 years later, this seasoned veteran quests ever still. Long ago, d’Artaud’s faithful steed died in battle, thus this brave knight fights on foot, defends the weak and helpless, and tirelessly seeks the Grail. He is such an inspiration upon the battlefield that those who fight beside him redouble their efforts, fighting even harder in his noble presence.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_anguille_factionleader}Having been a Sailor as a boy, Taubert denounces the idea of ever setting foot aboard any vessel. Instead of reigning at Castle L’Anguille, he prefers to reside in his lodge at Grasgar Castle, on the edge of the Forest of Arden taking the fight to any beastman warbands emerging from the Forest of Arden.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_anguille_first_2}Born of noble blood in Castle L’Anguille, Nedred de L’Anguille took more after his liege than most nobles in the castle. Nedred prefers to ride out on the hunt for beastman warherds rather than squabble about political messes and oversee logistics.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_anguille_first_3}An anomaly among Duke Taulbert’s retinue, Bayard Guillar prefers the logistical side when aiding his liege. Bayard makes frequent visits to Godemar Fitzgodric, the current steward of Castle L’Anguille, making sure that the city runs smoothly and the money flows into the Duke’s coffers.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_anguille_first_4}Having been found on the coast of L’Anguille by a small caravan of nobles making their way to Lyonesse, Albert de l’eau was raised by a couple who were of noble birth in Couronne. Many years into his training to become a knight of Bretonnia, Albert would accompany his adopted parents on a journey to L’Anguille where they would be ambushed by a beastman warband. Losing his adopted parents in the ambush, Albert had nowhere to go, so he pledged his fealty to Taubert, and now focuses his fury on the cursed inhabitants of the Arden.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_anguille_second_1}Leader of the Brethren of the Lighthouse, Godemar is a smart and intricate man, who worked his way up to becoming the steward of Castle L’Anguille. Although he is still in service to Duke Taubert, Godemar rules the city on his own with the help of his merchant Cabal. Many in his order, including himself, have thought about seceding from the rule of Duke Taubert, and even from the entire Kingdom of Bretonnia.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_anguille_second_2}Originally from the group that would found the settlement of Sigmarsheim, Ericht von Friesen would use his guile and merchant know-how to become the Corrupt Harbor Master of the Castle City of L’Anguille. Ericht oversees all trade, and personally takes a tax on all trade goods leaving and entering the city from the harbor.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_anguille_second_3}A born and bred sailor from L’Anguille, Nigel gets his nickname solely from his age, despite him being a senile and bitter man. Having lived in the city his entire life, Nigel knows the ins and outs of the entire city, and has eyes everywhere in every corner of the city. Nothing gets past ol’ Crusty.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_lyonesse_factionleader}Compared to most Nobles of Bretonnia, Adalhard de Lyonesse is a more simple man than most. He surpasses many knights on the battlefield, and enjoys the occasional feast and tournament. Adalhard however is not keen to the politics and scheming of many Bretonnian lords, instead deciding to march his army and resolve any political issues with a fight. Many of his vassals believe his true faith belongs to Ulric and not to the lady, but none of these “rumours” have been proven.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_lyonesse_first_2}Son of Duke Adalhard, Aldrad is a Knight of the Realm, having yet to venture on his Quest, believing that his father will soon pass on the Dukedom to him. Whispers have spread in Castle Lyonesse that Aldrad will instead be sent to La Maisontaal for unknown reasons, but that has yet to occur if they are to be believed.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_lyonesse_first_3}Shurlay is a mysterious noble within the court of Lyonesse, known for his enigmatic presence and unclear motives. While he has proven his loyalty, his origins are shrouded in secrecy, and he commands both fear and respect among the nobles. Shurlay is often seen in deep contemplation, plotting his next move in the intricate game of court politics.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_lyonesse_first_4}Known for his unwavering faith and noble demeanour, Philippe serves as a beacon of virtue and a staunch defender of the Lady's honour. His presence is marked by a serene confidence, inspiring those around him to strive for greater deeds. He leads a small but renowned regiment of knights known as the Knights of the Light.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_lyonesse_first_5}Henry the Red is a fierce and fiery warrior known for his bravery and tactical prowess, even for a knight of Bretonnia. With a reputation for bold tactics and unyielding spirit, Henry is a respected leader on the battlefield. His fiery temperament is matched only by his loyalty to the dukedom of Lyonesse, as well as being often called fancy by other nobles.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_lyonesse_first_6}Roland the Marshal is a knight of unmatched valour and honour. He wields the sword Durendal, said to be blessed by the Lady herself, and carries the olifant, a horn that can summon aid in times of dire need. Known for his unwavering loyalty and tactical genius, Roland is a beacon of chivalry in Lyonesse. His presence on the battlefield is both inspiring and fearsome, as he leads his troops with unmatched bravery.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_lyonesse_first_7}Orderic is a noble monk and scholar with a deep commitment to recording the history and culture of Lyonesse. Born to a noble family with both Bretonnian and Imperial roots, Orderic was sent to the abbey at a young age. His knowledge of both Bretonnian and Imperial cultures gives him a unique perspective, and his writings are highly regarded for their depth and accuracy. Orderic serves as the historian and advisor at Castle Lyonesse, often consulting ancient tomes and manuscripts to offer wisdom and guidance to the Duke.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_lyonesse_first_8}Born as a poor peasant girl in a small village in Lyonesse, Bertha was an outcast from her youth. Having each eye a different color, the superstitious people of Bretonnia treated her as an outcast and mistreated her. It was not until she was on the brink of death, when a vision of The Lady called her and she took her under her protection and granted her her gift. Today she is one of the most famous women in the duchy.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_artois_factionleader}The ruthless ruler of Artois, a giant of a man, stronger than any of his subjects. Chilfroy’s demeanour is often cold and grim, rumoured to only allow himself to smile when he surveys the battlefield after a victory, soaking in the bloodshed he has wrought. Chilfroy deals with courtroom cases swiftly, always picking the higher ranking side and punishing the losing side harshly. Because of this, people rarely take cases before the duke, which is the way he likes it, preferring to hunt wild beasts and the hated beastmen in the surrounding area, the pelts of which adorn the great hall of Artois.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_artois_first_2}A middle man who is slightly overweight and comes across as very pleasant, listening to people’s problems before passing judgement and doesn’t take pleasure in other people’s suffering. On the other hand, Tobias is a ruthless man, very quick to execute the guilty. Crippled criminals do not often make a useful contribution to society, after all. Tobias seeks to overthrow Chilfroy and become the duke of Artois, seeking to put his son on the throne.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_artois_first_3}Being the only son to Tobias Larret, his father is very protective of him and he’s lived a very sheltered life. Fredemund often works alongside his father, learning the way of the statesman, on the side he also practises with the blade in the hopes of one day becoming a grail knight. After much begging, his father has finally allowed him to ride out and lead a contingent of men.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_artois_first_4}A well travelled grail knight, Chlodegar’s fiefs are well defended, each fief has a grail chapel, which doubles up as a well defended fortification from which the defenders can hold out until help arrives. Chlodegar is an imposing man, his friendly demeanour hidden behind a disfigured face.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_artois_first_5}Sir Madregang used to be the lord of Uesin, but 5 years ago he ingested a potent skaven poison and began to mutate, followed by a skaven attack, Sir madegang was unperturbed by his mutations and fought the skaven back succesfully. while not a severe mutation, he was stripped of his title as lord but was allowed to remain a leader of men.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_artois_first_6}Sir Roul is the only man in the dukedom of Artois that Chilfroy trusts, he knows the reason that Chilfroy has become the cold man he is today. Before becoming the lord of the eastern lands of Artois, Sir Roul would frequently ride out with Chilfroy to destroy roving bands of beastmen, now he battles with the role of statesman and frequently holds court in Castle Béthune.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_artois_first_7}Lord Guiscard is an ox of a man, clad in armour he almost looks like a statue, and could fell a tree with one swipe of his blade. It is because of this that he has been granted lands in the southern parts of Artois, any incoming beastmen will meet a swift death at the hands of Lord Guiscard.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_gisoreux_factionleader}Duke Hagen of Gisoreux is uncompromisingly focused on upholding the laws of Chivalry, even past the norm for a grail knight. This status amongst the dukes of Bretonnia affords him much respect and admiration, to the point that even King Louen Leoncoeur began to seek out his advice on many matters. Today, Duke Hagen is one of the king’s closest companions and rarely if ever leaves his side. Recently it is said that he and his men-at-arms traveled into the darkness of Arden, facing down a whole coven of vampires and emerging victorious. Despite this outstanding feat, few make mention of it, it's said that of the men who ventured with him into Arden, that only the Duke returned.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_gisoreux_first_2}Marquis Frederic Desfleuve is a young man who has just recently been charged with the defense of Castle Desfleuve and the Gisoreux gap. His father died in a hunt recently, and his mother died in childbirth, leaving him as the last Desfleuve to carry on the blood line. Many rumors are circling the Marquis as apparently this has presented a major problem for him to address. The word is that he is seeking a trustworthy steward to help manage his affairs.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_gisoreux_first_3}A stern steward for a stern lord; many have truly suspected that Lord Hincmar and Duke Hagen are siblings both due to their similar attitudes and manners of speech. The reality is that Lord Steward Hincmar and Duke Hagen were childhood friends, and upon ascending the throne of Gisoreux, there was not a man in the world that Hagen could trust more than Hincmar.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_gisoreux_first_4}Earl Orlando is the lord of Castle Oisillon, and is charged with watching over the approaches towards the Pale Sisters from the Forest of Arden. The Earl is a distant relative of Duke Hagen and so his family’s heraldry is often mistaken for the duke’s. Where the duke has a Party per Pale Sable and Gules, an Argent Hart affronté, the earl has a Party per Pale Gules and Sable indented, an Or Hart affronté. Despite requests by the duke to modify the earl’s heraldry, thus far the duke has not conceded, likely due to the many benefits the Earl de Oisillon receives from this misunderstanding. Unlike his relative, Earl Orlando has never embarked on his grail quest.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_gisoreux_first_5}Sir Luidolf was not born in Gisoreux, though his family does hail from here. His heraldry tells the story; His father Sir Gunthar de Gisoreux met a fair maiden named Cunigunde in Mousillon. Her family having moved to that misbegotten land as part of the then King Feramand’s attempts to pacify the wayward dukedom. Accordingly, they adopted the dukedom’s Or field and Sable Fleur de Lys as their heraldry. Smitten by Cunigunde, Gunthar took her for his wife. When the Serpent of Mousillon drove out the last of the loyalist Bretonnians, Sir Gunthar was killed and his wife fled to Gisoreux with the babe Luidolf to the protection of her late husband’s family. As such Luidolf’s heraldry is Party per Pale Argent and Or bordered Gules, a Sable Hart passant toward Dexter, with a Sable Fleur de Lys chief sinister. Despite his origin laying in that cursed dukedom, many in Gisoreux love him, seeing him as a heroic prodigal son soon to begin his grail quest.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_gisoreux_first_6}A prodigious hunter, Sir Lothar is known to range the forest of Arden bordering on Gisoreux. It is said that he once shot a white hart, the symbol of Gisoreux, and mounted it in his hall. The next morning the mounted head had gone missing, but ever since then he has had unbelievable luck in both hunting and archery.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_br_lord_gisoreux_first_7}Brigitte is not only a damsel in the service of the Lady and the Duke of Gisoreux. She also has affairs with the elves and serves as an intermediary between both kingdoms. Although sources close to the duke suspect that he has greater sympathy with the elves than with Gisoreux itself. But these rumors have never been confirmed.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_factionleader}An enigmatic being, the Serpent of Mousillon is a dashing and heroic knight. He is a man who adheres to the principles that he was bound to as a knight of Bretonnia and is no less a fearsome warrior. As such, there is mercy to be shown in combat to knights of equal rank and prowess in combat. The Serpent will allow any he considers worthy to join his company. There is no mercy for any weak or incapable knights. Rumours claim that the Serpent of Mousillon is the long lost bastard son of Louen and has returned to reclaim what he believes is rightly his.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_first_1}Having a strong distaste for Mutants, Lord Rachard constantly scours surrounding lands for the untainted, choosing only to accept pure humans to reside within his villages.. If he does, however, find any mutants in his villages, it is said that they are taken to his castle and are never heard from again.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_first_2}The dark witch Lady Nicolette D'oisment was presumed dead 50 years ago but still reigns from the D'oisment tower despite all the whispers. Ever honing her dark skills on stolen children and rarely seen outside her tower, she has no plan of following the path of a regular daughter of Bretonnia, Instead she aids Mallobaude in his quest to take the throne.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_first_3}Ser Cain Bettencourt was once a noble questing knight of Bretonnia who had valiantly saved the damsel Josephine from a horde of Night Goblins. Unfortunately, after he had returned her to safety he was knocked unconscious from a toxin from the chief night goblin’s foul ‘stabba’. Being on the cusp of death, Ser Cain craweld into a small pond where a grail was there waiting for him. Unfortunately he did not know that the grail was false. Ser Cain survived his wounds and became a nightmare for the damsel he had saved, ever stalking her.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_first_4}Having fled from Sylvania, Gleb Marks is an prominent necromancer who backstabbed Manfred Von Carstein himself and ‘lived’ to tell the tale. Although hunted at every opportunity by both the living and the Von Carsteins, Gleb Marks has made his home with the famed Lord Rachard and has so far eluded all assassination attempts sent against him.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_first_5}Many assume Ser Garreth of the Black Rose is from the Imperial Order of the Black Rose, but it is far from the truth. Ser Garreth is an honourable sort when it comes to dealing with fellow Bretonnian Knights. Should anyone else challenge him, he will lose his composure. After every duel he wins against valiant foes, he offers his opponent a chance to become a fiend of the night. Those that refuse are buried with a blank headstone and are adorned with a black rose.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_first_6}Having long been a squire for the Serpent of Mousillon, Ser Agravain is an infamous black Grail Knight who has been a thorn in the side of Alberic de Bordeleaux. Known for leading raids into Bordeleaux time and time again, seeking unwilling servants for his master, Ser Agravain is a fearsome warrior who could stand up to most fabled Grail Champions, and has bested his brother in many practice duels.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_first_7}Although not as fearsome as his brother Ser Agravain the Shadow, Ser Gaheris the Dreaded is all the more cruel, and far more cunning. Being a Black grail knight himself, Ser Gaheris prefers tactics and strategy. Many raids from Ser Agravain the Shadow were led by by Ser Gaheris, and even many battles led by the Serpent of Mousillon himself. Ser Gaheris is a valiant warrior but is ever the more dangerous when on the sideline.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_first_8}Pitre Fonce, also known as the Madman of Mousillon, the very same who commanded the Nightguard, has returned from the dead to serve the Serpent of Mousillon on his Black Crusade against the noblemen of fair Bretonnia.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_first_9}Commanded by Pitre Fonce, the Black Duke led the army of the Restless Dead against all of his master's enemies. With Pitre now under service of the Serpent of Mousillon, the Black Duke commands the undead forces under the Serpents command.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_second_1}One of Mousillon’s most cultured nobles, Lord Aucassin comes from a long Line of Mousillonian nobles. His family supported Maldred’s civil war long ago as well as Duke Merovich’s war with Lyonesse. Although Aucassin is a great noble and indeed a great Bretonnian, he is also a bloodsucking creature of the night.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_second_2}Eustache is Mallobaude’s pet killer. He assassinates political and noble opponents of Mallobaude. Eustache also sometimes delivers theats, summons or ultimatums for Mallobaude, nobody dares to take it lightly. Eustache was once a strikingly handsome man but his years of fighting and crime gave him a hawk-like nose and hooded eyes now seem cruel. And now he is always sneering. Eustache’s skills with the blade is almost unmatched, but he has grown to employ more sinister methods, from stabbing victims in their bed to burning down their houses. Eustache self proclaimed nickname is Eustache of the Rusting Blade, a nickname he himself coined after being scolded by a fencing tutor as a boy for not looking after his blade properly. He uses the name to make sure he is always reminded that no matter how good a swordsman he is, there is always much he can learn about the art of death.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_second_3}A servant of the fell Vampire Aucassin, Gefrelar's duties involve leading hunts in the relatively sound countryside around the Château Hane, where guests are invited to shoot or Lance wild boar that have been specially imported and released into the Château’s grounds. Furthermore, he and his knights will often leave the Château to undertake mysterious missions, leaving only Aucassin and his household servants behind. This no doubt pertains to Mallobaude’s plot to take over the Dukedom.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_m_lord_mousillon_second_4}A Ghoulish Knight, Known for terrorising peasants and getting into conflicts more often then not. The Knight of the tower at Biaucaire is a feared man. A rumoured decendant of merovech, Ser Bougars De Biaucaire seeks to reclaim his families honour.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_factionleader}Many would envy Araloth for his position among the glade lords, the importance of Talsyn for the Asrai Realms is incomparable towards the others. Yet Araloth's decision often doesn’t just count for the good of Talsyn but the whole Athel Loren. After Orion and Ariel, he is often perceived as their first representative.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_first_2}As his Title suggests, Scarloc is known in and around all of Athel Loren. He is as famous among elves and humans, as he is feared by beastmen, who try to enter the forest. He uses his bow and stalks through the glades and woods, always ready to sneak upon the enemies of Athel Loren

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_second_1}For centuries Lady Tevaril fought the fight against the everlasting chaos in her realm, she fought the last battle against the hordes of Morghur. She remembers the Joy she felt when the Asrai won over the forces of chaos. Yet these days seem far away, the taint of the blood of Morghur confronts her with new abominations, loss and desperation.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_second_2}While Lady Delynna does all in her capabilities to reduce the corruption in Anmyr - at least tries to contain the corruption at a place, all her efforts seem fruitless. While the frustration grew, she started to consider new measures - even outside the realm of the Asrai. Her help requests went throughout the world, even to the Tower of Saphery in Ulthuan. When there is a way to stop the corruption, Delynna will find it.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_third_1}Sceolan fights as good with the bow as he does with his sword. Cloaked by the fog and snow of the region, his troops conducted masterful ambushes, and never found their way into the heart of Athel Loren

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_third_2}Beside the numerous wars and Lords Nemeru served through his lifetime, not much is known about him. He climbed the ranks of the Eternal Guard, until he became one of the leading commanders in Athel Loren.It is said that he still prefers to fight in the ranks of his men than commanding them.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_fourth_1}Argwylon is not only famous for its magic, but also their proximity to the mountains, where many Great eagles are present. The Asrai formed a strong bond with their flying neighbors and eventually were able to tame them. Thalandor Doomstar usally rides his Eagle “Gwandor”, together with his eagle he once flew over the forest by night hunting for goblins, which provided him his famous surname “Doomstar”

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_fourth_2}Lord Beldeas was once engaged with a spell weaver that was allowed due to his rank to serve the mage queen. She became the infamous fly queen that tricked and betrayed not only him but all of the Asrai, and were almost able to destroy the realm of the wood elves. The guilt he feels for the actions of his former wife, is haunting him till this day.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_fifth_1}Admadri is protecting the realm with all his strength. Unluckily for him, the enemies he tries to face sometimes arise from within, rather than outside the wood. Leaving him in a situation, hunting corrupted dryads or even demons of chaos, in the immediate vicinity of the feasts inside his realm.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_fifth_2}It is said that Lord Thuralin once fled with his child into Arranoc, and was creating a new living in this realm. In his past, he was romantically involved with a spell singer, which gave birth to his child. The spell weaver however, named Ordaana, lost the control over herself after the mage queen rejected her, and burned down her own glade. Luckily, Thuralin and the child could flee.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_sixth_1}Like his horseman, Edrael is a legendary rider. His skills are well known, even outside the realm yet other kin mostly try to avoid being with him. The daily confrontation with invaders in the wood, made him incredibly suspicious and prejudging… even against elves of other high realms.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_sixth_2}Valarion counts as one of the best riders of the Skymark Reaches. He is a skilled archer and rider at the same time and leads a warband of glade riders under his banner. He and his lord Edrael usually compete in horse races and hunting duels, competing for being the best rider of glades.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_seventh_1}Together with her Wildwood rangers, Lady Draya’s concern is mostly the defense from the evil tree spirits. It is no wonder she doesn’t like to talk a lot, especially to outsiders and even other forest spirits. For her, it often feels absurd how other Asrai fail to understand the other side of the forest spirits. Nevertheless her integrity to the rest of Athel Loren is not harmed by her daily business.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_seventh_2}Zeylin is one of the best Wildwood rangers Draya ever served. She trusts him enough that he is leading a Kitband of Wildwood rangers. While he is less reserved and sometimes even quite talkative, he shares the very same worries as her Lady.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_eighth_1}Lady Heggria is on par with her wardancer’s skills. Her coldblooded-ness and calculating manner however, allows her to lead the High realm, and control the focus of her dancers. She might therefore not be the most impressive dancer that seeks the ultimate challenge in combat, but she makes sure that all her dancers will find it and get a chance to demonstrate their abilities.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_eighth_2}Wychwethyl gained his title from the outstanding agility, quickness, and savagery during combat. He is one of the most exceptional Wardancers of Athel Loren. Every spring, Wychwethyl performs the ritual dance, for a new reign period of the King and Queen of Athel Loren.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_ninth_1}Untypical for the most wood elves, for Arias, there is only hate and envy and hunger for power. Why should his realm be the only one that did not recover from Ariel's phase of spreading corruption? A question he often asks himself in the silence of his dark throne room. For him, the other High realms are either too weak and cowardly to help him maintain control over the mid night glade, or they plan to fall on his back the moment he shows a sign of weakness. For both reasons, the Lord is isolating him more and more from the discussions of the Elven Courts.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_ninth_2}Morlanna spends most of her time studying Dhar, the Dark magic. She is probably the best Dark weaver on this side of the Ocean, on par with the Asrai’s cousins of Naggaroth. Her interest in the Dark side of Athel Loren, has ever grown.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_tenth_1}Lady Arda patrols pathways of the many moonstones of the high realm. While the harmony is rarely disturbed, whoever dares to do so will face death. In her rows every single guardian is learning from their beginning of their service, to protect the living, and respect the dead. After each battle, even outside her realm, fallen troops are respected with all honors after each and every fought battle, while a moon stone is prepared in their halls.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_tenth_2}Naneith knows the art of divination, a very rare and secret lore used upon the Asrai Spell weaver. Her power allows her to predict immediate dangers and sense the flow of magic deep in the ground of Athel Loren. She became so proficient in interpreting the signals of the future, that she is known among the Asrai as the Prophetess.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_eleventh_1}The legendary smith of the forges of Torgovann is blind yet, his work is the most outstanding craftsmanship any elf could see.It is said that Daith is the oldest elf ever existing. People date his works back to the creation of Armour of Aenarion of the first Phoenix King. With that, he is probably even older than Ariel and Orion. Neither his blindness, nor his age seem to affect his performance.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_eleventh_2}Calanoth made himself a name as one of the deadliest Warriors in the Forest of Loren. Originally, he was a wizard apprentice, who could make use of his talents when he and his master were ambushed by an orc warband. A few of his arrows are decorated with rubies which he only uses for his most worthy foes. It is said that he is still a magician, his powers just manifested in his bow.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_twelfth_1}Lord Findol is known to be a Masterful Ambusher. He is feared and admired for his tactical superiority inside the Asrai territory. Noteworthy, his attack on a dwarven treasure expedition of Grungi Goldfinger, left him with more foes than friends outside the woods. However, everyone who tries to trespass the woods, for his head or the treasures of Athel Loren, will knows that they could be seconds away from another ambush of the legendary Glade Lord.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_twelfth_2}While her husband is keeping invading forces away, Evelyne is ruling and organizing the realm of Wydrioth. As Devastating the Ambushes of her husband are, they require a lot of organization, coordination, and maintenance for hidden pathways. A circumstance, her husband often neglects, and even more important, that she is keeping her husband's back.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_thirteenth_1}Not as Fiery as her sister, Arahan is acting considerate, and prefers the dispute over combat. Nevertheless allows her rational stance to analyze and conclude the right tactical decisions in combat.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_we_lord_athel_loren_thirteenth_2}In contrast to her sister, Naestra is often said to embody the Dark nature of Ariel. She is impatient, impulsive and devious, and knows when it’s the best time to switch to the offensive, be in the dialogue, or hunt her enemies down.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_eo_lord_laurelorn_factionleader} Queen Marrsith is the fourth regent in Laurelorns 4000 year history. Her Great grandmother, Marvel, was Handmaiden to Ulthuan’s Everqueen when she was chosen by the High Council to become the Laurelorn’s first queen during the War of the Beard. Maruviel was the daughter of Aenarion’s first son Morelion, making Queen Marrisith a descendant of the first Phoenix King. Despite having ruled the Laurelorn for centuries, the queen is very much still young for elvish royal standards, having her delegate most of her authority to the much older High Council. Queen Marrsith also has the power of seeing the future, with Queen marrsith seeming to keep secrets of the portents she has experienced.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_eo_lord_laurelorn_first_2} Prince Aesryn is one who is steeped in jealousy over his Sister. To him, being the Queen (Or King) of Laurelorn should be a great responsibility. But from what Aesryn is seeing, that responsibility is delegated to the High Council, making Marrsith’s position more of a waste than anything. His jealousy set aside, Aesryn also wants to restore the Dragon Tower, an ancient remnant of the Elves, before the war of the beards. This time however, the tower would be cleansed from the arrogance of the Asur.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_eo_lord_laurelorn_first_3}Yadoh served Queen Marrisith for over 4000 years and is her oldest Champion. As her first champion in her rows, he experienced all troubles Laurelorn and the Eonir, from the Sundering, over the War of the Beards until the recent struggles against the chaos. In all these times, he was a loyal servant of his queen.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_eo_lord_laurelorn_second_1}The Kithbands of Galenstra guard the marshes of the Ward of the Rain since before the War of the Beards. His keen attitude and excellent knowledge of the terrain makes it almost impossible for the disorganized warbands of the beastmen or any other threat lurking in the south of Laurelorn to enter the forest.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_eo_lord_laurelorn_second_2}Elora father served as Lionguard of the Pheonix King As first offspring in the Laurelorn forest and finalizing the initial ritus, she is the first generation of her family being perceived as a Faniour, the forest born kindred of the Eonir. She learned from her father the traditions, the combat, and why there is no place for Asurian arrogance in the struggle for survival.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_eo_lord_laurelorn_second_3}Garelion is one of the patrol Captains protecting the southern part of the Laurelorn forest. Is quite a talkative individual when he is met on a campfire. He likes to visit a human tavern from now and then and is quite popular among the people. This changes quickly when he is sent on patrol missions in the swamps. Meeting him here could be your first and last encounter with him.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_eo_lord_laurelorn_third_1}Kaia is a powerful Spellcaster using her powers to oversee the Sea of Claws up the coast of Albion. Inhabitants of Nordlands and Norsemen gave her the infamous name Stormwitch which she accepts now as her own. She is calculating as she is beautiful. She takes her decision opportune. So it is not surprising she signed trading agreements with the druchis and rather sought peaceful interactions with norsemen. However whenever somebody tries to trick her they will understand why she is called the Storm witch.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_eo_lord_laurelorn_third_2}The Family of the Tide Striders, reach far back to northern Ulthuan province Cotique, which held thriving trade relations with the Asur colony which became Laurelorn. During the war of the beards, whenever the time allowed, Lord Adon went up the tower Se-Anthil, watched the shore and desperately watched out for the fleet of the Asur. However, their help never came, and everyday, he lost more hope in the Asur until a point he realizes that the Eonir better form their own kingdom. Today he smiles upon his naivety. He admires Kaia’s keenness, and sees no problem in the diplomatic exchange and trade with the Druchii.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_eo_lord_laurelorn_third_3}Flyson is usually occupied with many diplomatic missions around the world spending more time on foreign embassies and Courts of Asrai and Druchii, that he often is perceived as foreign and soft from the most of his kin. While indeed he has a weakness for good wine and the elegance of the world's courts, it is his silver tongue that resolved diplomatic issues and saved the existence of his people - which everyone appreciates.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_eo_lord_laurelorn_third_4}Altarion once was one of the most powerful archmages of Ulthuan. He was since the very beginning of his career interested in the nature of Dragons and how to tame them. Together with other Archmages of Caledor, he once tried to bind the creatures to their will, using the so-called ‘Fell Fangs’. This was perceived as an act of treason which led to him being expelled from the Asurian community and exiled to Laurelorn forest. Like many other of the expelled ‘Greylords’, he built himself a residence somewhere in the Silverwood, where he continued his experiments. When Altharion is not busy with his studies, he somewhat grows an interest in keeping pesking forces away from his laboratories, which let him help the Warden of the Sun from time to time. Which makes him an unusual and selfish - but also powerful ally of the Eonir.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_eo_lord_laurelorn_fourth_1}While Lindialoc is keeping strong trade ties with the Government of Salzenmünd, he is also the one putting tensions into these relations. He disobeys direct decisions originating from the High Council just to achieve additional concessions that benefit the elves. While he certainly does not win supporters in the High Council, the elves do admire his cunning to achieve Laurelorn’s Interest in the Empire of Men.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_eo_lord_laurelorn_fourth_2}There are secrets in Laurelorn, which seldomly belong in nobody else's hands than those who owe to protect them.The hermit Athanoc is tired of his burden. Yet he doesn’t anybody to gain knowledge about the magic of athel loren.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_eo_lord_laurelorn_fourth_3}Iyana is leading a Kithband of Eonir Warriors, defending her homeland against the Norse invaders. While she is disillusioned that laurelorn ever shines as it did centuries ago, she is practical, inventive, and adapts to the situation her people are living in. She has good relations with human locals around the Wardens and rather appreciates their support, than seeing them as invaders of Laurelorn.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_factionleader}Ungrim Ironfist is the Slayer King of Karak Kadrin. There has never before been a Dwarf more torn between his duties than Ungrim Ironfist. As the King of Karak Kadrin, he is oathbound to protect his kingdom and his people. As the patriarch of the Angrulok Clan, he has to ensure that his relatives succeed, and as a sworn Slayer who has taken the oath, Ungrim is also bound to seek his doom against the most powerful foe he can find. Never content to sit back on his throne and wait, Ungrim looks for any opportunity to lead his throngs to war. There are few kinds of monsters that walk the world that Ungrim Ironfist has not slain in battle. Armed with the enormous Axe of Dargo, Ungrim deals death, carving a path of red ruin before him while singing songs of old in a booming voice. Atop his head is a bright orange crest that rises above a sturdy horned helmet set with a golden crown. For Ungrim is both a Slayer and a King, more than likely the last of the line of Slayer Kings of Karak Kadrin.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_first_2}Dorin Flamebeard is a living embodiment of vengeance, his fiery orange beard streaked with soot and ash as if reflecting the blazing inferno of his wrath. Once a proud warrior of Karak Kadrin, Dorin swore the Slayer Oath after failing to save his kin from a devastating Greenskin raid that left an entire mining outpost in ruins. Now, he roams the battlefields seeking redemption in death, though none have yet been able to grant him the release he craves. Dorin wields a giant greataxe, its edge glowing faintly red as if kissed by the forge. His bare chest is a canvas of scars, each one a testament to battles fought against trolls, wyverns, and even a dreaded Chimera. Dorin’s ferocity in combat is unmatched, his movements a whirlwind of strikes that leave foes in pieces before they can react. His fiery demeanour matches his appearance; he is quick to anger but equally quick to inspire those who fight alongside him. Among the Slayers of Karak Kadrin, Dorin is revered as a hero, even if he rejects such accolades. For him, every battle is a step closer to the redemption he seeks but has yet to find.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_first_3}Ulfar Stonebane is a towering figure among the Slayers of Karak Kadrin, his immense frame and booming voice making him a presence that cannot be ignored. Before taking the Slayer Oath, Ulfar was a miner of great renown, known for his ability to carve through solid stone with unparalleled speed and precision. His path to dishonour came when he led his mining crew into a cavern infested with Skaven, resulting in the loss of many lives, including his younger brother. Wracked with guilt, he swore to seek a glorious death in battle. Ulfar wields a massive two-handed war axe, its edge engraved with runes of destruction that amplify the force of his strikes. His fighting style is as relentless as an avalanche, crushing everything in his path with devastating swings. His sheer physical power allows him to go toe-to-toe with some of the largest foes, from Chaos Trolls to the towering beasts of the Ogre Kingdoms. Despite his grim purpose, Ulfar has a deep, booming laugh that echoes through the halls of Karak Kadrin, and he often shares tales of his battles over tankards of ale.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_first_4}Skaldi Doomshard is a grim and brooding figure, his face half-covered in burn scars from a failed attempt to slay a Hellcannon of Chaos that had laid waste to a Dwarf outpost. Though he succeeded in destroying the infernal war machine, the magical backlash from its destruction left him disfigured and filled with a deep-seated hatred for the forces of Chaos. From that day forward, Skaldi has dedicated his life to hunting daemons and their mortal servants, his every strike fuelled by a burning desire for vengeance. Skaldi’s weapon of choice is a great axe, its blade etched with ancient runes of warding and banishment. The weapon is said to hum faintly in the presence of Chaos, guiding Skaldi’s strikes with uncanny precision. Unlike many Slayers, Skaldi is not prone to boisterousness or revelry. He is a solitary figure, often seen sharpening his axe or muttering ancient oaths under his breath. His dour demeanour and single-minded focus on his task make him an intimidating presence, even among his fellow Slayers. Despite this, Skaldi is respected for his unyielding determination and his ability to face even the most horrific foes without flinching. Among the halls of Karak Kadrin, his name is whispered with a mixture of awe and sorrow, for Skaldi Doomshard is a Slayer whose path is paved with fire and blood.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_first_5}In the halls of Karak Kadrin, where the echoes of oaths and battle cries fill the air, one Dwarf stands apart, not as a Slayer, but as their guide and keeper of the ancient arts. Runelord Thori Runescorch is no outcast, nor does he seek the glorious death the Slayers crave, yet he walks among them as a mentor, a smith, and a force that pushes them beyond their limits. Clad in thick gromril armour etched with radiant runes of fire and might, Thori embodies the fury of the forge, a flame that drives the Slayers ever forward. Unlike many of his kin, Thori does not scorn the Slayers for their choice. Instead, he sees them as Dwarfs who have embraced the most dangerous path a son of Grungni can take. It is his duty, then, to ensure that when they march to battle, they do so wielding weapons and blessings worthy of their sacrifice. From his forge beneath Karak Kadrin’s great hall, he inscribes burning runes onto axes, hammers, and even the flesh of willing Slayers, igniting their wrath to new heights. His 'Runes of the Forgeheart' sear into their weapons, making them burn like the heart of a volcano, while his 'Runes of the Phoenix' infuse the Slayers with an unyielding fire that keeps them fighting even through wounds that would fell lesser warriors.Thori himself is no mere smith, nor does he hide in the safety of the hold. In battle, he wields a rune-etched hammer that leaves trails of fire in its wake, each strike bursting into flames that sear foes to cinders. He stands at the threshold between the living and the dead, ensuring that no Slayer’s sacrifice is in vain. Though he does not seek his own doom, he will not shirk from battle, and should his death come, he knows it will be in service to his kin.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_first_6}In the annals of Karak Kadrin, few Slayers have carved a path of destruction as fearsome as Hengist Doomcleaver. A grim and towering figure, his body is a patchwork of scars, each wound a testament to a battle fought and a foe slain. His once-golden beard is now streaked with crimson from the endless slaughter, and his piercing gaze burns with the embers of vengeance. Hengist has hunted daemons for decades, cleaving through their twisted forms with his Greataxe, inscribed with runes of banishment that sever the unnatural ties that bind them to the mortal realm. Hengist does not revel in battle like some of his Slayer kin; he treats it as a duty, a debt to be repaid in blood for some long-forgotten disgrace. He does not boast, nor does he drink in the halls of Karak Kadrin, for his oath consumes him utterly. When daemons pour forth from rifts or corrupted lands, it is Hengist who leads the charge, cutting them down like a reaper at harvest. To see him in battle is to witness a storm of steel and blood, his axe flashing in great arcs, each swing driving back the tide of the unnatural. Though he seeks his end, fate has denied him time and again. He has faced greater daemons and survived, his hatred burning ever fiercer. The Doomcleaver walks a path from which there is no return, and until he falls, he will continue carving his name into the annals of Karak Kadrin in the blood of the damned.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_first_7}Rurik Earthshaker was once a king’s champion, a warrior of unmatched skill who stood beside Karak Kadrin’s rulers in times of war. But betrayal and failure tainted his honour, and so he cast aside his title, his riches, and his pride, swearing himself to the Slayer’s Oath. From that day forth, he became a slayer who sought out only the most fearsome and monstrous foes to earn his redemption Unlike many Slayers who fight alone, Rurik leads bands of his kin into battle, carving through the horrors of the world in a whirlwind of blood and fire. His weapon is a mighty great axe inscribed with runes of ruin, and its edge burns with white-hot fury when turned against the creatures of Chaos. He has hunted across the Worlds Edge Mountains and beyond, facing greater daemons, mutated dragonspawn, and creatures of nightmare that few would dare name aloud.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_first_8}Among the Slayers of Karak Kadrin, Urist Ironbane is a legend whispered in awe and dread alike. His very name is a curse upon the dark forces of Chaos, for no daemon, beast, or monster has yet managed to lay him low. It is not for lack of trying, Urist has hurled himself into battles that should have claimed his life a hundred times over. Yet each time, he emerges, bloodied but unbowed, his mighty Waraxe still swinging with undiminished wrath. Urist’s path to the Slayer cult was paved in sorrow and ruin. Once the lord of a great hold now lost to the tides of Chaos, he swore his oath after witnessing his kin slaughtered, his halls desecrated, and his legacy reduced to nothing. But his death did not come as he had hoped. Every battle he fought should have claimed him, yet fate seemed to mock his suffering, keeping him alive even against overwhelming odds. He has faced daemons of Khorne in single combat, endured the warpfire of Tzeentch’s horrors, and stood against a Verminlord with nothing but his bare hands, and still he lives. Many whisper that Urist is cursed, that his doom will never come, and that he is fated to wander the earth as a Slayer who will never die. Whatever the truth, the Undying Slayer fights on, his hatred undimmed, his wrath eternal. Perhaps one day, he will meet his end at the hands of a foe truly worthy of his fury, but until that day, the enemies of the Dawi will tremble before his name.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_first_9}Once among the most respected thanes of Karak Kadrin, Bolli Vorgrun stood as the unyielding rock upon which countless enemy assaults were shattered. A warrior of indomitable spirit and steadfast discipline, Bolli spent decades defending the Slayer Keep’s outer fortifications, holding the walls against the greenskin hordes, Chaos warbands, and the monstrosities that threatened the ancestral home of Grimnir’s chosen. He was a shield-brother to kings, a hammer that never faltered, and a voice of wisdom in the feasting halls. But even the strongest stones can crack. In the last great siege of Karak Kadrin, Bolli led a vanguard force to break the lines of a Chaos incursion led by a monstrous warlord. The battle raged for days, and though Bolli and his warriors fought with unrelenting fury, their position was overrun. He was left for dead amid the bodies of his slain comrades, the sight of his warriors being torn apart forever etched into his memory. When he awoke, he was among the survivors, those who had failed to hold the line. The shame was too great to bear. He cast aside his rank and his duties, swearing the Slayer's Oath in silent fury. But fate had other plans. King Ungrim Ironfist himself intervened, declaring that Bolli was not meant to walk the Slayer’s path, but that of a warrior-lord, one who would bring ruin to the foes of the Dawi with the rage of a Slayer and the discipline of a Thane. And so, Bolli fights on, clad in his rune-inscribed gromril armour, bearing his mighty shield which has turned aside blows from daemon lords and dragonfire alike. No longer a Thane, but something more, a living bastion of Karak Kadrin, sworn to defend his hold until the very mountains crumble.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_first_10}The tunnels and mines beneath Karak Kadrin stretch deeper than most dare to tread, and in those dark, winding passages, one name carries the weight of legend, Dori Magrest. A miner-lord of unmatched skill, he has spent his life in the depths of the earth, carving through stone to uncover hidden riches, lost vaults, and long-forgotten paths. Where others see rock and ruin, Dori sees the veins of the mountain, knowing where to dig and when to hold. Born into a long line of miners, Dori’s name was spoken in reverence even before he took up lordship. His hammer is no mere tool of labour but a rune-etched relic that has struck down both stone and enemy alike. He led countless expeditions into the underways, unearthing lost Dawi relics and recovering the wealth of Karak Kadrin’s ancestors. Yet, it was his battle against the Skaven of Clan Mors that cemented his place in history. When a massive tunnel collapse left his mining party trapped, he led them in a desperate defence, fending off hordes of chittering vermin in the pitch-black darkness. With naught but pickaxes and sheer determination, Dori and his kin fought their way to the surface, dragging Skaven corpses behind them as proof of their defiance. Now, as a lord of Karak Kadrin, Dori commands the mountain’s depths, ensuring its wealth remains untapped by the enemy. He has reforged ancient passageways, strengthened collapsed tunnels, and even uncovered long-lost chambers of runic knowledge. But he is no mere overseer, when the time for battle comes, Dori wields his hammer with the same force he would strike a stubborn ore vein, shattering skulls with the might of the mountain itself.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_second_1}Dorin Silverfoot, son of Haakon Hargrimsson, is a noble Dwarf lord of ancient lineage, descended from the once-proud hold of Karaz Bryn, now lost to the Pale Lady’s cursed dominion. Born amidst exile and raised among the dispossessed. As a young warrior, Dorin’s life was torn apart when a Greenskin warband descended upon his encampment. His entire family was slaughtered, yet by some miracle, or the will of the Ancestor gods, Dorin survived, found unconscious in the remains of a bloodied tent, surrounded by the mangled corpses of Orcs and Goblins. While he lingered on the edge of death, the priests who looked over the dead discerned something unusual in the lad. Upon consulting the ancient genealogies and rune-stones, they uncovered a truth long buried: Dorin was of royal blood, a direct descendant of Razek Silverfoot, Thane of Karaz Bryn and son of King Borri Silverfoot. When Dorin awoke, he found the healers, warriors, and even the priests bowing before him. From that day forward, his destiny changed. Trained by the finest warriors among the dispossessed clans, Dorin proved a gifted and determined pupil, rising swiftly through their ranks until he bested his own master in single combat. With axe and shield, he earned not only respect but also loyalty. Now recognised as a lord and leader, Dorin Haakonsson leads daring raids into the blighted lands near Karak Ungor and Karaz Bryn, harassing enemy patrols, reclaiming long-lost mines, and reforging the pride of his fallen people. Though cautious and calculating, Dorin bears a simmering resolve; he knows the time draws near when the Dawi shall march to reclaim Karak Ungor. And after that, his path will lead to Karaz Bryn itself and the reckoning that awaits within its cursed halls.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_second_2}Furgil Emberkeeper is the last surviving Runelord of Karaz Bryn, the once-proud hold now lost to shadow and undeath. A master of ancient lore and sacred craft, Furgil earned his name during the doomed final days of the hold, when he gathered the most precious relics of his people, the sacred rune-scrolls, oath-stones, and a shard of the hold's Eternal Forge-fire, and led a desperate retreat through crumbling halls and bloodied tunnels. Many fell in the retreat, runesmiths torn apart by rampaging Greenskins, others dragged screaming into the dark by the Pale Queen’s cursed minions, but Furgil endured. Scarred, wearied, and burdened by loss, he now leads a cadre of loyal runesmiths in exile, teaching them the forgotten rune-lore of Karaz Bryn and fuelling in them the fire of vengeance. Though older than stone and grimmer than iron, Furgil’s skill at the forge has not waned. Each weapon he crafts is a masterpiece of wrath and remembrance: blades etched with runes to keep the dead from rising, warhammers that strike with the fury of the ancestors, and blessed axes to cleave through troll-hide in a single blow. These are no mere tools of war; they are heirlooms of a grudge not yet settled. Furgil has sworn a mighty oath: he shall not pass into the halls of his forebears until Karaz Bryn is reclaimed and the Pale Queen burns in its forge like the cursed abomination she is. It is for this reason, with a heavy heart and reluctant hand, that Furgil now lends his knowledge to weaken the corrupted rune-wards that still bolster Karak Ungor’s walls. He does so not for glory, but because he sees no other path forward. The sooner Karak Ungor falls, the sooner the great reckoning can begin, and Furgil Emberkeeper will be there to see it done.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_second_3}Kazgar Bonecleaver was once a proud warrior of Karaz Bryn, until the cursed day the hold fell to the Pale Lady and her undead host. In the choking darkness of a desecrated shrine deep beneath the earth, Kazgar was forced to watch as his wife and children were sacrificed upon a foreign, rune-scarred altar. He would have struck then and there, roaring with grief and fury, but fate had other plans. A Dwarfen rescue party dragged him away screaming, while the Pale Lady's cruel laughter echoed through the caverns like a taunt from some forgotten nightmare. Broken in spirit and consumed by wrath, Kazgar refused to rejoin his surviving kin. Instead, he made the long and bitter trek to Karak Kadrin, where he took the Slayer's Oath before the ancestors. No longer a warrior of a hold but a seeker of a glorious death, Kazgar wandered far and wide, westward to battle the shambling horrors of the dead and northward to clash with the daemons and beasts of Chaos. Yet no foe, no wound, no fury could grant him the release he sought. He did not die. And in every fitful sleep, the Pale Lady’s laughter haunted him still. Now, Kazgar has returned, his mind fraying like an old banner in the wind, his body a patchwork of scars and half-healed wounds. Reunited with the remnants of his kin, he has decided to use their lands as a base of operations. From their redoubts, he launches relentless raids into the cursed depths of Karaz Bryn, seeking one thing and one thing only: to silence the laughter.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_second_4}Vragni is as old as the mountains are grey and among the last living Dwarfs who still remember the fall of Karak Ungor. He was there when the hold's garrison made its final, desperate stand against the greenskin tide from below. Though the warriors fought with grim valour, with their backs against the walls and without the main host of Karak Ungor to reinforce them, they could not stem the horde. Knowing the hold was lost, Vragni sounded the retreat, guiding the survivors out the gates and into the southern reaches of Karak Kadrin. King Morek Stonehammer never forgave him for this outrage. When the old king perished, Vragni became an advisor to the scattered lords and stewards of the displaced clans. But as the years ground on, his words grew fewer, and his counsel was less sought. Whether from grief, shame, or the slow wear of time, Vragni's voice faded from the halls of leadership. Now, Vragni lives only to fight and drink, burying the old pain in battle and ale. On the field, he is a masterful commander, silent, watchful, and possessed of a battlefield instinct bordering on the supernatural. His warriors move with uncanny precision, often taking up complex formations at the utterance of a single gruff word. In silence, Vragni has found his purpose once more.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_second_5}Thori Shattershield is a battle-hardened lord of Karak Ungor, born and raised in exile among the scattered remnants of his fallen hold. Though denied the stone halls of his ancestors, Thori was forged in the hardship and bitterness of the wilderness, his resolve tempered by the unrelenting struggle for survival against greenskins, undead, and worse. His name was earned during a brutal ambush upon a caravan of exiled clans. In the heart of the melee, Thori came face-to-face with a hulking Orc warboss. The two clashed in single combat, and though Thori was eventually disarmed, he refused to yield. With a roar, he shattered his heavy oaken shield against the beast’s skull, caving it in and felling the brute where it stood. The remaining Orcs, leaderless and stunned, broke and fled into the hills. Since that day, the name Shattershield has been spoken with respect among the exiles of Karak Ungor. Thori has become a symbol of their enduring defiance, leading raids into the lost hold’s outer tunnels and vowing that the day of reckoning will come when the kin of Karak Ungor march once more beneath the mountain.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_second_6}Haming the Rock, once mockingly known as Haming the Wazzok, is a Dwarf lord of Karaz Bryn, renowned not for wit or wisdom, but for indomitable strength and unshakable resolve. Taller and broader than most of his kin, Haming's intellect is not his strongest asset, a fact he acknowledges without shame. He wisely entrusts the finer details of command and drill to his more sharp-minded subordinates. Tasked with the grim duty of reclaiming an old mine infested by the undead, one the Pale Lady had attempted to retake using her minions, Haming led a force to both cleanse the tunnels and rescue any surviving miners still trapped within. During the assault, Haming was separated from his warband while battling a towering undead giant. As he fought his way through the gloom, he came upon a narrow chamber where a group of young miners had been cornered against a wall, a shambling horde of skeletal and rotting horrors closing in. Without hesitation, Haming threw himself into the breach, wedging his massive bulk between the undead and his kin. He held the narrow corridor alone, a wall of iron and fury, enduring blow after blow as the miners slipped past him to safety. Rotten clubs and rusted blades alike broke against his armour, but he would not fall. Not while a single Dwarf remained in danger. When his unit finally caught up with him, they found Haming battered, bloodied, and breathing heavily, yet still standing. The dead lay in heaps at his feet. He said nothing, but the cheers and laughter of his kin told him all he needed to know. From that day forth, none have dared call him a Wazzok. Now he is Haming the Rock, the immovable shield of Karaz Bryn, and he swears that all who threaten his kin shall be ground to gristle beneath his boots.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_second_7}Norgrim the Lost is a grim and haunted lord of Karak Ungor, known amongst the clans as much for his uncanny survival as for the mystery that shrouds his past. Once thought slain during the fall of Karak Ungor, Norgrim vanished beneath the mountain as the greenskins poured through its tunnels. For decades, no word of him reached the exiled clans, until he emerged, gaunt and battle-worn, bearing scars both seen and unseen. None know precisely where Norgrim spent those long years. Some whisper he wandered the deepest holds alone, hunting the greenskins that defiled his ancestral home. Others claim he walked the winding, cursed tunnels of the World’s Edge beneath the notice of gods or daemons. A few even say he died, and that what returned is not quite Dwarf. What is known is this: Norgrim returned changed. His eyes burn with a quiet fury, and his voice carries the weight of ancient grief. He speaks little of what he endured, save to mutter darkly of the 'echoing silence' and the 'things that dwell where even the Thaggoraki will not.' He bears an heirloom axe, once thought lost with Karak Ungor, and a tattered banner which he refuses to let any other Dwarf touch. Norgrim has become a rallying figure for those who dream of reclaiming the lost hold. He leads sorties with cold precision and relentless purpose, striking at goblin encampments and cursed crypts alike, ever drawing closer to the gates of Karak Ungor. To his foes, he is a vengeful shadow from the deep. To his kin, he is a symbol of endurance and vengeance, the Dwarf who was lost, and who will stop at nothing to see his home reclaimed.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kadrin_second_8}Mendri Blackpowder is an eccentric and sharp-witted Engineer of Karak Ungor descent, born and raised in exile amidst the scattered remnants of the lost hold’s clans. Charged with the fabrication and upkeep of siege engines and blackpowder weaponry, Mendri serves as a vital cog in the efforts to sustain and advance the military might of the displaced Dwarfs of Karak Ungor and Karaz Bryn. In the long years of exile, resources have been scarce and machinery scarcer still. Mendri and his fellow Engineers have been forced to innovate, repair, and repurpose old weaponry with dwindling supplies, always struggling to keep the forges burning and the guns firing. Yet, in Mendri’s inventive mind, frustration breeds ambition, and ambition, in turn, has birthed a radical solution. Where others see the unbreachable walls and impenetrable gates of Karak Ungor, Mendri sees a flaw to be exploited. He argues, with wild gesticulations and blackpowder-laced breath, that the hold cannot be retaken by conventional means. Decades of failed assaults prove as much. His proposal? Blow it up. Explosives placed in key locations in the hold, the walls and the tunnels would collapse a large part of the city, bury its enemies beneath it, and leave nothing for the greenskins to crawl back to. In his mind this would kill a large part of the greenskins and force the rest to retreat underground, with the tunnels collapsing behind them, allowing the Dwarfs to march right in from the surface. The lords and Thanes scoffed, of course. Some called him mad. Others, worse. But as the years drag on, more have begun to wonder, in hushed tones and dark chambers, whether madness might not, in fact, be genius. Mendri Blackpowder waits, blueprint in hand and powder dry, for the day his plan is given its chance. And when that day comes, the earth shall tremble.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_angazhar_factionleader}Duregar, King of Karak Angazhar and patriarch of Clan Branmakaz, has long stood as a stalwart protector of Black Fire Pass. For many decades, he commanded the defences that held the mountain pass against countless incursions. In more recent years, however, he has passed this responsibility to his son, Baragor, entrusting him with the fortress’s continued vigilance. Now focused primarily on overseeing the hold’s trade and the management of its wealth, Duregar nonetheless remains a warrior-king at heart. He frequently leads sorties into the surrounding regions, seeking to settle grudges recorded in the Angazhar Kron. His hatred for the Grobi runs particularly deep; ever since a cunning raid saw a tribe of Night Goblins plunder one of Karak Angazhar’s obsidian mines, he has harboured a personal vendetta against their kind. Their use of cowardly trickery to abscond with cartloads of precious obsidian remains a black mark in the king’s memory, and one he swears to avenge in full.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_angazhar_first_2}Baragor has proven his mettle time and again, earning the respect of warriors and Thanes alike. Yet despite the fame of Karak Angazhar’s obsidian axes, he steadfastly refuses to wield one. Instead, he places his trust in the oldest allies of the Dwarfs, iron and steel. It was iron and steel that defended Black Fire Pass for centuries, and in Baragor’s eyes, it shall be iron and steel that continue to do so. A staunch traditionalist, Baragor views many of the Engineers’ Guild’s more recent innovations with open scepticism. Guns, he admits, have their place, but what good are black powder and gearwork when the true glory lies in hearing a thrice-blessed suit of armour ring out as an Urki blade shatters upon it? To Baragor, the Dawi’s strength lies not in inventions, but in honour, endurance, and cold-forged steel.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_angazhar_first_3}Harek Grimbeard is a revered Longbeard of Karak Angazhar, his name etched with honour in the hold’s records following the infamous Battle of the Gap. During that dark hour, a violent collapse within the Underway tunnels severed Harek from his unit. Trapped behind the rubble with naught but a handful of miners, he found himself standing alone against the skittering tide of goblins that poured forth from the darkness. A narrow gap between two mounds of stone was all that separated the beleaguered miners from the enemy. Harek planted himself in that breach like an iron-banded wall, shield high and axe flashing in the gloom. Goblin blades struck from every angle, clawed hands grasped through the gap, but none made it past the old warrior. Using the confined space to his advantage, Harek held the line with grim determination, felling countless Grobi with each swing. It was only when reinforcements finally broke through the flanks that the goblins were driven back into the shadows. Though wounded and weary, Harek stood tall amidst the carnage, his armour slick with gore and his beard stiff with blood.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_angazhar_first_4}When a young clan-dwarf first emerges from the mines and takes up his inaugural az, it is tradition that he does not do so alone. Though the Dwarfs are many things; stubborn, proud, and unyielding, reckless is not one of them. No beardling is sent to war without guidance, for even the stoutest heart must be tempered by experience. That is where Drong Steelpick comes in. Drong commands a company of hardened veterans and wide-eyed beardlings, leading them into their first battles upon the surface. His role is not simply that of a warrior, but a teacher, ensuring that the young Dwarfs learn not just how to swing an axe, but how to survive. Under Drong’s watchful eye, beardlings learn to hold the line, to read an enemy’s movements, and to trust the shield beside them. Stoic and battle-worn, Drong has marched against Beastmen, Greenskins, and worse, always returning with fewer in his ranks but stronger warriors beside him. His presence is both reassuring and immovable, a living bulwark who teaches through example. Many a famed Thane once swung their first axe under Drong’s command.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_angazhar_first_5}Alf Thomsson is the current captain of the Ebonshard Brotherhood, an elite fighting force renowned for wielding axes edged with obsidian, mined from the depths beneath Karak Angazhar. Though the blades are brittle and difficult to forge, they are razor-sharp and deadly in the hands of seasoned warriors. As captain, Alf oversees all aspects of the Brotherhood’s upkeep: from rigorous training schedules and strict quality control of weaponry, to ensuring that the company sees regular combat. He is also responsible for identifying promising warriors from other units who might one day be deemed worthy of joining the Brotherhood. However, the final decision rests with the king, for admittance into the Ebonshard ranks is not given lightly. The Brotherhood is composed almost entirely of veterans, and younger members are a rarity. Alf himself is the oldest of them all, a grim and respected figure who has cut down countless foes in defence of the hold.
