Though age weighs on his shoulders, his blows are still as precise and brutal as ever. His voice carries great weight in matters of war, and his presence alone can steady even the most uncertain shield line.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_angazhar_first_6}Runelord Garil Stoneforged presides over the ancient forges of Karak Angazhar, where the famed obsidian-bladed axes of the hold are crafted. Alongside his squad of master Runesmiths, Garil painstakingly inscribes runes of sharpness upon each weapon, ensuring that they bite through armour and bone with an edge no natural forge could provide. Unlike many of his order who remain within the sanctity of the forge halls, Garil often marches to war alongside a company of the Ebonshard Brotherhood. There, amidst the roar of battle, he observes the potency of his rune-craft firsthand. With every clash of blade and shield, he adjusts and reinforces the runes with grim precision, channelling ancient power through hammer and chant to strengthen the might of Dwarf-forged steel in the very heart of battle.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_angazhar_first_7}Sven Whitemane is a respected elder of Karak Angazhar, a grim and steadfast Dwarf who lost most of his kin in a brutal Greenskin raid. Stricken with grief and fuelled by righteous fury, he has since dedicated the remainder of his days to the destruction of the enemies of the Karaz Ankor.Though he once stood upon the precipice of taking the Slayer's Oath and seeking an honourable death in battle, Sven chose a different path. Instead, he now leads a company of dispossessed Clans Dwarfs, fellow Dawi who, like him, have suffered great loss. Together, they form a vengeful warband whose purpose is not redemption through death, but the reaping of a grim toll upon those who would threaten Dwarfkind.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_angazhar_first_8}Kallon Silverbreaker is a renowned Dwarf Lord of Karak Angazhar. A calculating and brooding strategist, Kallon is best known for his mastery of defensive warfare.He stood beside Prince Baragor Sharpblade during the defence of Black Fire Pass, when a vast Greenskin horde sought to force its way through. Reinforcements from the Empire were sparse, Averland’s mad Count failed to recognise the true scale of the threat, dismissing the warnings as Dwarfen exaggeration. Undeterred, Kallon made do with what forces he had, employing tactics seldom seen by either Dwarf or Man. His personal unorthodox strategies turned the tide.The battle was won with minimal loss of Dwarfen or Imperial life, and the Greenskins were driven from the pass.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_angazhar_first_9}The brawler-king of Karak Angazhar, Logan Hammerfist is as renowned for his iron fists as he is for consuming copious amounts of alcohol, even by Dwarfen standards. A towering figure among his kin, Logan’s brawny frame and scarred, calloused knuckles speak of decades spent in brutal close combat, both on the battlefield and in the tavern. His punch, it is said, lands with the force of a warhammer’s swing, capable of shattering a troll’s skull. He is rarely seen without his ancestral gauntlets, Grimdrengi, forged in the hold’s deepest forges and inscribed with runes to channel and enhance his prodigious strength. Though he is a fearsome warrior, Logan’s true love lies in the camaraderie of the feast hall, where tales of glory flow as freely as the ale. Quick to laugh and quicker to anger, he is a steadfast ally, a fierce champion of his hold, and a deadly foe to any who would threaten Karak Angazhar.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_angazhar_first_10}Durgin Galazbar is a venerable Dwarf Lord, his name etched into the annals of Karak Angazhar with runes of honour and remembrance. Clad in thick Gromril plate, adorned with runes of spell-breaking, his armour is a masterwork of Dwarfen craft, rendering him near-impervious to foul magic and capable of withstanding the crushing blows of giants. Renowned for his unyielding resolve and immovable stance, Durgin has long stood as a bulwark against the Greenskin menace, a living shield between his hold and the darkness. Though his beard is long and grey with age, his strength has not waned, and his wisdom is as keen as the edge of a rune-forged axe.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_azgaraz_factionleader}King Thuringar Orc-Hewer unexpectedly ascended to the throne fifty years ago, following the assassination of both his father and elder brother. Since that grim day, King Thuringar has vowed to bring war to the Greenskins and drive them from the Grey Mountains once and for all. Many tribes have already fallen beneath the steel plated boots of his throngs, yet the task of securing the entire range remains long and arduous. Within the Inner Council, opinion is divided. Some hail the king’s campaign as righteous vengeance, while others question the wisdom of such prolonged warfare against a foe that breeds like vermin and strikes from the shadows.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_azgaraz_first_2}Ganmar Oakheart is the commander of the Ranger Corps of Karak Azgaraz. He seizes every opportunity to venture beyond the hold, whether on scouting missions or in dealings with the Wood Elves. Most dwarfs regard Ganmar’s fondness for the outside world as highly eccentric, if not outright peculiar. His company is composed almost entirely of rangers, like-minded folk who share his affinity for the wilds and a deep mistrust of civilization beyond stone walls and mountain halls.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_azgaraz_first_3}Harok, ruling lord of Clan Steelcrag of Karak Azgaraz, is a master of siegecraft, both defensive and offensive. Under his command, numerous greenskin raids have been repelled, only to be answered thrice over by thunderous volleys from the hold’s cannons and grudge-throwers. Harok is renowned for his meticulous planning and unrelenting resolve, forging a reputation among friend and foe alike as an unshakeable bulwark of Dwarfen warfare.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_azgaraz_first_4}Morek Flintbeard is the ruling lord of Clan Flintbeard of Karak Azgaraz, a clan famed for its mastery of close combat and known across the Grey Mountains as the 'Hammer of Karak Azgaraz'. While Hammerers are traditionally sworn to the king’s personal guard, Clan Flintbeard has earned the rare honour of maintaining its own elite unit of Hammerers, warriors who favour aggressive assaults over the usual defensive formations, often fighting shoulder to shoulder with their lord. Morek himself is a formidable warrior, proficient in a variety of melee weapons, some of which are unfamiliar even to other dwarfs. Yet he remains true to Dwarfen steel, bearing into battle a mighty warhammer of ancient make. He maintains strong ties with the Runesmiths of Clan Thunderstone, and his armour is inscribed with powerful runes of endurance and spell-breaking.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_azgaraz_first_5}Kazrik Cragtooth is the ruling lord of Clan Cragtooth of Karak Azgaraz, a venerable clan whose lineage traces back to the Dragonback Mountains and the lost hold of Ekrund. Once a high-standing warrior clan, they earned lasting honour by covering the retreat of other Dawi during Ekrund’s fall, an act of grim bravery that cost many lives. Though the hold was lost, the Cragtooths endured, and have since dedicated themselves to vengeance, seizing every opportunity to strike against the hated greenskins and vile Skaven. Kazrik himself is a stoic and unyielding figure, known for his iron resolve and unwavering commitment to the defence of the hold. So long as a Cragtooth draws breath, no more dwarf holds shall fall.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_azgaraz_first_6}Ketil Ironarm is the ruling lord of Clan Ironarm of Karak Azgaraz, one of the founding clans of the hold. Though steeped in tradition and martial pride, the clan is often the subject of jest among other dwarfs, largely due to their perceived arrogance. Some, with beards safely out of reach, even liken them to High Elves, though never to their faces, of course. Mockery aside, few can deny the strength of Clan Ironarm, known for fielding stalwart ranks of Ironbreakers in battle. Ketil himself, mockingly called Angelgi behind his back, is the most boastful of them all, and has left more than a few taverns in ruin over a slight to his honour. Still, none can call him a braggart without cause. Ketil is ever at the vanguard, letting the enemy break upon him and his kin, his armour drenched in gore and glory alike. Even so, many in the hold wouldn’t mind seeing him taken down a peg, or three.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_azgaraz_first_7}Durak Irebeard is the ruling lord of Clan Irebeard of Karak Azgaraz, one of the founding clans of the hold. Once a proud and fiery lord, Durak took the Slayer’s oath following a grievous dishonour, though he has never spoken of the event that led him to it. Despite becoming a Slayer, he retains his authority within the clan, a rare but not unheard of situation among the dwarfs of the Karaz Ankor. Durak’s rage is the stuff of legend. His roaring voice echoes through the hold, and his presence in battle is nothing short of terrifying. He hurls himself at the largest and most dangerous foes, seeking a glorious end worthy of song and remembrance. Many of Clan Irebeard have followed in his footsteps, their numbers among the Slayers swelling in recent decades. Though Durak still leads them in battle, it is clear he fights not for power or pride, but to redeem a shame he refuses to name.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_azgaraz_first_8}Ruling Lord of Clan Grimhelm of Karak Azgaraz, one of the founding clans of the hold. Skalf is a Dwarf whose grim visage is as much a part of his identity as the rune-carved helm he bears into battle. As the Lord of Clan Grimhelm, he upholds the clan’s reputation for stoic resilience and unwavering loyalty to Karak Azgaraz His helm, wrought from darkened gromril and adorned with runes of defiance, is a revered heirloom said to have withstood the crushing blows of giants and the foul sorcery of dark wizards alike.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_azgaraz_first_9}Proud leader of Clan Falconshield, Kallon’s name is synonymous with mastery of the skies and the unyielding defence of his kin. Clad in gleaming gromril plate, he wields a finely wrought war axe and a rune-etched shield said to have turned aside the blades of Greenskin warlords and the claws of Chaos beasts alike. His shield, known as Skyguard, is a revered heirloom of his clan, forged by the Runesmiths of Karak Azgaraz and imbued with runes of protection and resilience. Though a lord of iron discipline and unshakable resolve, Kallon is also a skilled falconer, and his heart soars with the same freedom as his birds. He is often found in the high crags above the hold, releasing his falcons to wheel and dive in the mountain winds, their cries echoing across the peaks. These birds serve not only as companions but as scouts and messengers for the hold, their keen eyes and swift wings offering early warning of any approaching threat.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_azgaraz_first_10}The venerable Runelord of Clan Thunder-Stone stands as a living testament to the enduring might and craftsmanship of the Dwarfs of Karak Azgaraz. With a beard as white as mountain snow, braided with rune-inscribed bands, Grundi’s visage is one of ancient wisdom and unyielding resolve. His rune-etched armour gleams faintly with the light of protective wards, each rune inscribed with the meticulous precision born of centuries of practice. He bears the ancestral weapon of his clan, a mighty warhammer whose head is hewn from enchanted granite and crackles with runic energy that echoes the fury of a lightning storm. When wielded in battle, it strikes with the force of an avalanche, casting enemies aside like leaves upon the wind. To stand against Grundi Thunder-Stone is to face the wrath of the mountains themselves, a fury that no foe, however formidable, has yet endured and lived to tell of it.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_eksfilaz_factionleader}The venerable king of Karak Eksfilaz and ruler of clan steelclad. His gromril armour, handed down through countless generations, is etched with runes of protection and endurance, shimmering faintly with the power of his ancestors. Each dent and scratch tells a tale of battles fought and grudges avenged. Hergar seeks to expand further west and south to increase his influence, there are very few greenskin tribes this side of the vaults, but the skaven are in over abundance, which is why expansion has to be carefully planned. The skaven have ignored the insignificant hold for now, but if they expand too quickly, they might draw the skaven into a war the dwarfs cannot win, even with their human allies. Hergar himself is a traditionalist, as the hold can ill afford the maintenance of guns and cannons, and relies heavily on his quarrelers and and grudge throwers to make up for their lack of firepower.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_eksfilaz_first_2}Durmin Ironscribe is the spiritual and arcane heart of Karak Eksfilaz. As Master of the hold’s ancient forge, he wields the sacred art of rune-craft, inscribing powerful runes upon weapons, armour, and even the gates of the hold itself. A figure of immense wisdom, Durmin’s long beard is braided with threads of silver and gold, each braid symbolising a rune he has mastered over a lifetime of study and devotion. A staunch guardian of tradition, Durmin ensures that the ancient lore of the Dwarfs is neither lost nor diluted, passing it down to the next generation with unwavering precision. Karak Eksfilaz possesses few Runesmiths, and those it does have are trained extensively, for only the finest may carry the sacred craft. Owing to the hold’s scarcity of rich ores, Durmin has become a master of his craft, capable of inscribing runes even upon common iron, imbuing it with strength and resilience to rival gromril itself. Under his watchful eye, even the humblest blade may become a weapon worthy of song and saga.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_eksfilaz_first_3}Lord and reigning Champion of Karak Eksfilaz, Durnik Stonefist is a warrior of unmatched prowess and a living legend among his kin. Towering over most Dwarfs, his formidable frame is the result of decades of unrelenting training and hard-won battles. Each year, Karak Eksfilaz hosts the famed Clash of Clans, a brutal contest of strength in which only the lords of the clans may compete. Durnik has claimed victory thirteen years in a row, his dominance undisputed. Though the King is permitted to take part, he has abstained ever since the infamous Broken Skull incident, an event spoken of in hushed tones and grim chuckles, choosing instead to preside over the games as host.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_eksfilaz_first_4}Master of the mines within Karak Eksfilaz, Finn Deepdelver is charged with the oversight and safe expansion of the hold’s tunnels through the Vaults, as well as the establishment of new mines in search of precious ore. Though possessed of a gruff and taciturn demeanour, Finn holds a deep and abiding care for his miners. He has, on more than one occasion, placed himself in grave danger to pull his kin from the rubble of collapsed shafts or to fend off sudden greenskin ambushes in the dark.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_eksfilaz_first_5}Lord Brogg Ironthane is a paragon of Dwarfen resilience, a stalwart defender of Karak Eksfilaz who commands respect with every measured step of his iron-shod boots. His towering frame, by Dwarfen standards, is encased in a suit of armour so intricately wrought, it is said to have taken a full century to complete. Brogg’s presence upon the battlefield serves as a rallying cry for his kin; his booming voice, like the tolling of a great bell, stirs even the most battle-weary warriors to rise and fight anew. In the aftermath of battle, he is often found within the great halls of Karak Eksfilaz, recounting tales of the ancestors and raising a tankard in their honour. Yet, behind his steely exterior lies a heart weighed down by the losses his clan has endured through centuries of unrelenting war.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_eksfilaz_first_6}Dwinbar Underforge, the Flamebearer of Karak Eksfilaz, is a figure wreathed in both mystery and fire. His long, braided beard, streaked with the ash-grey of age, is bound with golden clasps shaped like tongues of flame. His armour, an intricate mosaic of bronze and steel, shimmers with the heat of runes. These ancient and potent inscriptions allow him to channel fire itself in battle, reducing his foes to cinders with a single swing of his hammer. Born into the Underforge line, Dwinbar’s affinity for flame and metal was evident from a young age. As a youth, he spent countless hours in the forges of Karak Eksfilaz, learning the secrets of the ancestors who first mastered the art of binding fire to steel. Despite his fiery demeanour, Dwinbar is a deeply introspective Dwarf. He often retreats to the Forge of Ancestral Flames, a sacred chamber within Karak Eksfilaz, to commune with the spirits of his forebears. There, he crafts weapons and armour of unparalleled quality, each piece imbued with the enduring essence of his lineage.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_eksfilaz_first_7}Fimbur Frostbeard, the Winter’s Sentinel, is the living embodiment of the cold, unyielding strength of the mountains. His beard, white as freshly fallen snow, flows down to his belt, secured with bands of silver and frost-crystals. His armour gleams with an icy sheen, its surface perpetually cold to the touch. Crafted from a rare alloy found only in the deepest mines of Kraka Drak, it is said to be impervious to both flame and frost. Fimbur wields a warhammer forged from glacial ice and bound with runes of eternal cold. When swung, the weapon leaves a trail of frost in the air, and its impact can freeze foes solid. His mastery of the chill extends beyond his weapon; his very presence seems to leech warmth from the air, sapping the strength of his enemies and fortifying his kin. Fimbur yearns to one day return north to help his kin fight against the armies of chaos.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_eksfilaz_first_8}Grimbold Stonecleaver, the Shield of the Deep, is a towering figure whose very presence exudes an aura of unshakeable strength. His beard, a cascade of dark grey, is woven with iron clasps bearing the sigils of his clan. His armour is a marvel of engineering, layered with interlocking plates that offer unmatched protection without sacrificing mobility. His shield is as tall as a man and as unyielding as the mountains themselves. Grimbold’s weapon of choice is a massive handaxe, a relic passed down through his family for generations. The blade, etched with runes of impact, is capable of splitting even the hardest stone with a single swing. In battle, Grimbold is a bastion of defence, standing firm against even the most ferocious assaults. His shield wall is the stuff of legend, a formation that has withstood countless sieges and charges.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_eksfilaz_first_9}Lord Guttri Ironsunder is a figure of grim determination and unrelenting resolve, embodying the stoic endurance of the Dwarfs of Karak Eksfilaz. His beard, black as coal and streaked with the grey of age, is bound with iron clasps shaped like shattered anvils, symbols of his clan’s enduring strength in the face of adversity. Guttri’s armour is forged from fragments of ancient Dwarfen artefacts, reforged into a suit that gleams with a dull, unyielding sheen. Each plate is etched with runes of defiance, granting him resilience against both blade and sorcery. Born into the Ironsunder line, Guttri has always borne the weight of his ancestors’ grudges with fierce pride. His clan, renowned for its mastery of siegecraft and fortification, has long served as the backbone of Karak Eksfilaz’s defences. Guttri himself has overseen the construction of countless battlements and redoubts, each a silent testament to his skill, foresight, and unbreakable will.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_eksfilaz_first_10}Lord Thungi Stonehammer is a towering figure among the Dwarfs of Karak Eksfilaz, his presence as solid and enduring as the mountains themselves. His beard, a deep auburn streaked with silver, flows down to his chest, bound with clasps of polished granite and gold. His armour is a masterpiece of Dwarfen craftsmanship, its surface engraved with intricate depictions of mountain ranges and ancient runes of stability. Thungi’s weapon of choice is a massive warhammer hewn from a single block of enchanted granite. The hammer’s head is inscribed with runes of impact, each blow capable of shattering stone or hurling foes from their feet. Thungi is a deeply spiritual Dwarf, often found within the Temple of Grungni, where he offers prayers in thanks for the bounty of the mountains. His steadfast faith and enduring wisdom make him a trusted advisor to King Hergar Steelclad, and his voice carries great weight in the council chambers of Karak Eksfilaz.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_gantuk_factionleader}King Skag Hammerfist, the stalwart ruler of Karak Gantuk, is a Dwarf of unmatched resilience and strength. His massive frame is clad in a suit of ancient gromril armour, adorned with runes of warding and endurance, forged by the finest Runesmiths of the hold in ages past. His beard, a deep iron-grey streaked with white, is braided and bound with silver rings, each a mark of a great victory or a defining moment in his reign. Skag’s weapon is a colossal warhammer etched with runes of shattering and impact. Passed down through generations of kings, it becomes in Skag’s hands the symbol of his unbreakable will. On the battlefield, King Skag is a force of nature, his hammer crushing through armour and bone alike, his booming voice rallying the warriors of Gantuk to fight with unyielding resolve.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_gantuk_first_2}Runelord Thrandin Stoneforge is one of the most revered figures in Karak Gantuk, a master of the ancient and sacred art of rune magic. His beard, long and fiery red, is bound with golden clasps shaped like anvils, and his eyes burn with the intensity of a forge-fire. Thrandin’s armour is etched with runes of warding and spell-breaking, rendering him a bulwark against sorcery and the dark arts. He wields a rune-inscribed hammer of formidable power, each swing unleashes a burst of searing energy, capable of sunder­ing enemy lines or burning through enchanted barriers. Ever at his side is the Book of the Forge, an ancient tome containing the secrets of his craft, its pages consulted with reverence before new runes are inscribed or their potent magics invoked.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_gantuk_first_3}Lord Brond Deepstone, master of Karak Gantuk’s mines, is a grizzled veteran of countless expeditions into the mountain’s shadowed depths. His beard, black as coal and streaked with silver, is bound with steel clasps shaped like pickaxes. Brond’s armour is reinforced with stone-plated segments and etched with runes of fortitude, enabling him to endure the crushing pressures of the deep earth. He wields a colossal pickaxe forged from enchanted steel, capable of cleaving through stone and enemy armour with equal ease. On the battlefield, Brond strikes with the precision of a master miner, each blow measured, deliberate, and devastating, aimed to exploit the weaknesses of his foes with ruthless efficiency.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_gantuk_first_4}Lord Durn Wavebreaker is the stalwart commander of Karak Gantuk’s shieldwall, a figure of iron resolve and unyielding discipline. His beard, dark brown and streaked with grey, is braided and bound with bronze clasps shaped like shields, symbols of his unwavering commitment to defence. Durn’s armour is engraved with runes of protection, rendering him all but impervious to harm. He bears a towering shield reinforced with Gromril, its surface scarred by a hundred battles. In the crucible of war, Durn leads from the front, his shield the anchor of the Dwarfen line, his axe hewing down any foe bold enough to test his mettle. A resolute defender of Karak Gantuk, Durn’s leadership has turned back countless invasions. His warriors follow him without question, for they know he will never falter, never yield, and never leave a comrade behind.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_gantuk_first_5}Lord Harrin Goldbeard is the master of Karak Gantuk’s treasury, a shrewd and calculating Dwarf with a gaze sharp as a jeweller’s lens and a mind honed for matters of coin and craft. His beard, a gleaming cascade of gold, is bound with rings of platinum and studded with gemstones, each a testament to his success and status. His armour, inscribed with runes of prosperity and resilience, marks him as the guardian of the hold’s wealth and fiscal strength. Harrin wields an ornate axe forged from enchanted gold, its blade etched with runes of sharpness, both a symbol of his authority and a weapon of deadly efficiency. Though his focus lies with the ledgers and vaults, Harrin is no stranger to battle; when the time comes, his strikes are measured, precise, and lethal.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_gantuk_first_6}Lord Kargan Ironheart is the Warden of Karak Gantuk’s gates, a grim, unyielding Dwarf who bears his duty with unflinching resolve. His beard, black streaked with grey, is bound with iron clasps shaped like ancient keys, symbolising his role as keeper of the hold. Kargan’s armour, engraved with runes of endurance, renders him near-immovable, an unbreakable bulwark against all who would assail the gates. He wields a massive maul, forged to crush those foolish enough to test the strength of Karak Gantuk’s defences. Tireless and ever-watchful, Kargan inspects the fortifications daily, ensuring that every wall stands firm and every gate is sealed tight against the darkness beyond.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_gantuk_first_7}Lord Garin Thunderhammer is the master of Karak Gantuk’s artillery, a position he upholds with the zeal of a true engineer and the precision of a seasoned tactician. His beard, grey and flecked with soot, is bound with clasps shaped like cannonballs, a mark of his lifelong devotion to the art of war. Garin’s armour, reinforced with runes of resistance, shields him from the blasts and shrapnel that accompany his volatile craft. He wields a warhammer forged from Gromril and etched with runes of shattering, the hammer strikes with the concussive force of a cannonball. Each blow lands with a resounding boom, splintering shields and shaking enemy ranks to their core. As a commander, Garin is both meticulous and inventive, ever seeking new ways to harness the destructive might of his war machines. Yet his fury is legendary, swift and unrelenting, should his beloved artillery be misused, neglected, or placed in jeopardy.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_gantuk_first_8}Lord Throngrim Anvilborn is a living legend among the Dwarfs of Karak Gantuk, a warrior whose name is spoken with reverence and awe in every hearth and hall. His beard, a deep brown bound with bronze clasps shaped like axes, reflects his status as a master of war. Throngrim’s armour is a masterpiece of Dwarfen craftsmanship: a thick suit composed of interlocking layers of iron and steel, engraved with runes of protection and strength, enabling him to endure even the most brutal of onslaughts. He wields a rune-inscribed axe, striking with terrifying speed and precision. Etched with runes of sharpness and fury, the weapon carves through enemy ranks as if they were parchment. Throngrim’s fighting style is a fearsome blend of discipline and savagery, refined through countless battles against Greenskins, Skaven, and the darkspawn of Chaos. As a leader, Throngrim is both unyielding and inspirational. His thunderous voice echoes across the battlefield, stirring the hearts of his kin and urging them to fight with the wrath of the ancestors. His presence alone is enough to rally wavering lines, and his deeds are immortalised in sagas and stone within the halls of Karak Gantuk. Off the battlefield, Throngrim is a staunch traditionalist, fiercely devoted to the ancient customs and values of his people. He dedicates his time to training the next generation of warriors, ensuring that the martial legacy of Karak Gantuk remains as enduring as the mountains themselves.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_gantuk_first_9}Lord Dorrin Stonehearth is the steadfast keeper of Karak Gantuk’s hearth and home, a noble whose focus lies in the defence and prosperity of the hold’s inner sanctums. His beard, a rich auburn streaked with grey, is adorned with clasps shaped like hearthstones, symbolising his unwavering commitment to the safety and well-being of his kin. Dorrin’s armour is a marvel of Dwarfen craftsmanship, inscribed with runes of resilience and fortitude, ensuring he stands firm against any threat that dares breach the hold’s walls. He wields a rune-etched warhammer that embodies the enduring spirit of Karak Gantuk’s hearthfires. Imbued with runes of striking and endurance, the weapon delivers crushing blows while imbuing nearby allies with a sense of unity and steadfast resolve. As a leader, Dorrin is pragmatic and fiercely protective of his folk. He oversees the daily workings of the hold, its forges, granaries, and mines, ensuring all run with Dwarfen precision and order. In times of war, he commands the Hearthguard: a veteran unit of warriors sworn to defend the inner halls and sacred places of the hold. Dorrin is deeply respected for his wisdom and patience, qualities that make him a trusted counsellor to King Skag Hammerfist. His voice carries weight in the council chambers, where he champions strategies that temper aggression with the enduring preservation of Karak Gantuk’s strength.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_gantuk_first_10}Lord Varrik Dúmdrengi is a figure of grim determination and searing resolve, a Daemon Slayer who has risen to a position of leadership not through lineage, but by deeds of unmatched savagery and valour. His beard, once a proud auburn, now burns a fiery orange, dyed in the Slayer tradition and bound with iron clasps shaped like runic flames. His bare chest is a testament to his trials, marked with scars and tattoos, each a record of a mighty foe vanquished in his relentless quest for a glorious death. Varrik bears a colossal axe inscribed with ancient runes of destruction. The weapon is said to burn with an inner fire, its edge capable of cleaving through the armoured hides of Chaos champions and even the ethereal flesh of daemons. His strikes land with terrifying force, driven by a Slayer’s unyielding fury and a burning thirst for redemption. Though an unconventional lord, Varrik commands the respect of his kin through sheer force of will and the magnitude of his deeds. He leads a grim brotherhood of Slayers who have sworn themselves to his cause, oath-bound warriors united in vengeance, bound to walk the path of ruin until their doom is earned. Varrik’s presence in Karak Gantuk is both a source of inspiration and unease. To many, he embodies the very essence of Dwarfen wrath and resilience, a living legend who will not bow, even before death itself.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_hirn_factionleader}Alrik Ranulfsson is regarded as something of an oddity, even amongst a race as steeped in custom and tradition as the Dwarfs, for his near-fanatical devotion to the ways of his forebears. Despite the increasing need to deal with other races for trade and diplomacy, Alrik has held fast to the ancient customs of his people, refusing to yield an inch to modernisation. His armies are composed of warriors and Ironbreakers, supported by Quarrellers and Grudge-Throwers, echoing the proud formations of old. He has little time for newfangled contraptions such as Flame Cannons and Gyrocopters, viewing them as unproven distractions from tried-and-true methods of war. Alrik is even more of a traditionalist than his father, Ranulf, and has taken it upon himself to pursue the settling of every wrong inscribed within Karak Hirn’s Book of Grudges. With grim determination, he wages war against Greenskins, Skaven, and even Elves, demanding recompense in blood for ancient slights and betrayals. While all Dwarfs are taught the bitterness of grievance, few pursue vengeance with the same relentless fervour as Alrik. He has already struck out an entire volume of grudges, but the book is thick, and many pages still remain.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_hirn_first_2}Prince Gorrin Alriksson, son of King Alrik Ranulfsson, stands apart from many of his kin through temperament as much as deed. Where his father is stern and steeped in the old ways, Gorrin is possessed of a more even-handed nature, an inheritance from his mother, whose calm judgement and open-mindedness left a lasting mark upon the young prince as he grew up. Gorrin bears the heavy burden of representing his hold to the outside world. Unlike many of his kin, he does not look down upon other races. While never forgetful of the grudges his people carry, he is willing to speak with Elves and treat with Humans, seeing in them not just allies of convenience, but peoples with whom mutual respect, and even friendship, might be forged. Though some in the council chambers grumble at his modern learnings, none can deny that Gorrin’s efforts have opened valuable trade routes, eased tensions with nearby settlements, and brought honour to Karak Hirn through his skill in negotiation. Calm where his father is fierce, measured where others bristle, Gorrin may yet be the future his hold needs in a world ever darkening with war.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_hirn_first_3}Hamnir once fought as a mercenary in Tilea, hired by a noble who laid claim to the lands of a rival. The wars of the southern realms are often petty and short-lived, little more than skirmishes or single-day battles, but they are no less real for it. Steel is drawn, lives are lost, and reputations are forged in blood. Though many dismiss these conflicts as play-fighting for the bored sons of the nobility, the deaths are no less real. Lords from across the Old World send their heirs to the Tilean wars to earn their scars and temper their pride, and the Dwarfs are no exception. Hamnir was one such noble. Arrogant and untested, he entered the fray seeking glory, but found instead the hard lessons of humility, hardship, and brotherhood in battle. His years in Tilea were not merely for experience, but for the forging of a truer character, one that understood the weight of command, the sting of loss, and the value of comradeship.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_hirn_first_4}Skalf Ironpeak is a Dwarf Lord of towering stature and indomitable will. His beard, braided into intricate patterns, gleams with silver and gold, a testament to his high standing as the very pinnacle of Dwarven nobility. Clad in a suit of rune-inscribed Gromril armour, Skalf embodies the unyielding resilience of his kin, standing firm against any threat to his hold. He wields a great hammer forged in the deepest forges of Karak Hirn, a weapon of ancient power. Its runes shimmer with arcane might, and each strike delivers a crushing blow capable of breaking even the most formidable of foes. Yet Skalf is more than a warrior, he is a diplomat and steward of his people, balancing the needs of Karak Hirn with the interests of the greater Dwarven realms and, at times, even those of the Empire. When a trading caravan or emissary manages to brave the perilous mountain paths leading to Karak Hirn, they are often greeted by Skalf himself, flanked by a retinue of honour guards, a gesture of both hospitality and strength.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_hirn_first_5}Runelord Drumin Stonecarver is the revered master of Karak Hirn’s runesmithing halls, a venerable Dwarf whose command of rune magic is unmatched across the mountains. His beard, streaked with white, is bound with bands of gold inscribed with ancestral symbols, while his eyes burn with the fire of centuries spent in relentless study and sacred toil. Drumin’s armour is adorned with warding runes that shimmer faintly with a bluish hue, a quiet but constant testament to the power of his craft. He wields a mighty rune-hammer, used both upon the anvil and upon the battlefield. The head of the hammer is etched with runes of Breaking and Binding, allowing Drumin to shatter enemy enchantments with a single blow or to bolster the resolve of his kin when the tide of battle threatens to turn.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_hirn_first_6}Lord Durrin Granitefist is the stalwart commander of Karak Hirn’s Ironbreakers, a seasoned warrior whose courage and martial prowess are the stuff of legend. His beard is dark and thick, braided with clasps of tempered steel, while his gromril armour bears the scars of countless campaigns fought beneath the mountain’s shadow. Durrin wields a rune-etched axe, its edge capable of sundering even the most formidable of defences. In battle, he leads with unshakable resolve, forming an unbreakable wall of shields that has repelled countless greenskin hordes and Beastmen incursions. Though gruff and uncompromising, Durrin is fiercely loyal to his king and kin, earning the unwavering respect of all who march beneath his banner.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_hirn_first_7}Vikram Grimflame is a Daemon Slayer whose deeds have secured him a place in the annals of Karak Hirn’s storied history. His fiery orange hair and beard, bound with iron bands, stand in stark contrast to the grim resolve etched into his battle-worn features. Vikram wields a massive rune-axe, its blade inscribed with runes of flame, capable of incinerating daemonic foes with every strike. His body bears the marks of countless battles, scarred flesh and sacred tattoos, each one a testament to a victory won against the unholy forces of Chaos.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_hirn_first_8}Manrak Ironspike, a venerable lord of Karak Hirn, stands as the unyielding guardian of the hold’s southern approaches. Renowned for his iron resolve and masterful defensive strategies, Manrak has weathered countless assaults from Greenskin warbands and Beastman raiders amidst the rugged peaks. Clad in ancestral armour engraved with intricate runes of fortitude, he bears a massive shield forged from meteoric iron and wields a rune-etched warhammer that has laid low innumerable foes. Though ever the stalwart defender, Manrak harbours a simmering hatred for the Ogres who prowl the mountain passes. He dreams of one day leading a great muster to drive them out entirely, reclaiming the lost trade routes and securing Karak Hirn’s supremacy over the southern mountains.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_hirn_first_9}Durin Rockhewer is a masterful miner and renowned delver, famed for uncovering long-lost vaults and hidden chambers deep within the roots of Karak Hirn. As Keeper of the Lost Vaults, Durin oversees the mining expeditions that fuel the hold’s wealth and keep its forges burning with unyielding fire. His appearance is as rugged as the mountains he carves. His beard, streaked with grey and coal dust, is braided with bands of silver, each one marking a discovery of note. He wears a helm hewn from black granite and a cloak fashioned from the hides of cave-beasts, tokens of his many forays into the forgotten deeps. Durin is a deeply superstitious soul, often seeking the counsel of Runelords before embarking on major delvings. He holds a firm belief that the mountains whisper to those willing to listen. and more than once, his uncanny intuition has spared his crews from cave-ins, lurking beasts, or worse.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_hirn_first_10}Balin Stormpeak is a formidable figure within Karak Hirn, renowned for his mastery of mountain warfare and an unyielding will as enduring as the peaks he defends. For decades, Balin has safeguarded the vital trade routes and treacherous mountain passes that link Karak Hirn to the wider world. Though a battle-hardened warrior, Balin is also a tactician of considerable reputation. He is a master of ambush and terrain manipulation, expertly turning the unforgiving landscape of the mountains to his advantage. Many would-be invaders have found their doom amidst rockfalls and hidden kill-zones, their plans undone by Balin’s cunning stratagems. Despite his martial prowess, Balin is a staunch advocate of diplomacy and trade, recognising the strategic value of Karak Hirn’s role as a bastion of commerce. He is often called upon to mediate disputes between neighbouring holds and human settlements, earning him respect even beyond the mountain's shadow.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_izor_factionleader}Kazran Grimbrow is the King of Karak Izor and is a formidable figure among the nobility, his thick, grey-streaked beard braided with silver clasps, and his brow set in a perpetual scowl of grim determination. Clad in gleaming gromril armour inscribed with runes of resilience and prosperity, Kazran bears himself with the solemn weight of a king whose every decree shapes the destiny of his hold. His crown, a masterwork of silver and gold set with diamonds, is said to have been forged by the first Runelords of Karak Izor, an enduring symbol of his clan’s unbroken lineage. Kazran wields an ancient rune-axe passed down through generations of Clan Izorgrung’s rulers. The weapon serves as both a symbol of kingship and an instrument of war, its blade etched with runes of sharpness and vengeance that gleam with an otherworldly light. In battle, Kazran is a fearsome sight, his strikes precise and unrelenting, his mere presence enough to stir the hearts of his warriors and drive them to renewed feats of valour.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_izor_first_2}Lord Thori Goldhammer is a stalwart lord of Karak Izor, a master of both diplomacy and war. He oversees the extraction and refinement of precious metals and gemstones, safeguarding the prosperity of his kin. Thori’s armour is a dazzling masterpiece of gromril, inlaid with silver and gold filigree, a testament to Karak Izor’s wealth and craftsmanship. His weapon of choice is a rune-axe of peerless make, rumoured to strike with the precision of a jeweller’s chisel. Though a warrior of renown, Thori is also a shrewd negotiator. He has forged enduring alliances with nearby holds and human realms, ensuring Karak Izor remains a vital nexus of trade and a rival in influence to Karak Hirn. Yet he is no stranger to battle; his axe has slain countless Greenskins and Skaven who dared encroach upon the hold’s treasures. His leadership is defined by balance, tempered by wisdom, yet unyielding in the face of adversity.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_izor_first_3}Brokk Silverwright is the venerable Runelord of Karak Izor, a figure of immense reverence and awe. With a beard as white as freshly fallen snow and eyes that gleam like molten silver, Brokk embodies the ancient wisdom of the Dwarfen race. Clad in rune-etched gromril armour, he bears a mighty hammer that serves as an extension of his indomitable will. Brokk’s mastery of rune magic is the stuff of legend, and many of Karak Izor’s most prized heirlooms bear the mark of his craftsmanship. His presence on the battlefield is as heartening as it is decisive, his runes of warding and resilience have turned the tide of countless engagements. Despite his great age, Brokk remains a staunch defender of the hold, often marching alongside his kin to ensure his runes are wielded with the honour and purpose for which they were forged.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_izor_first_4}Hugnir Firemane is a figure of grim legend within Karak Izor, a Daemon Slayer whose fiery beard and burning gaze are said to mirror the fury of the Ancestors themselves. Once a proud warrior of the hold, Hugnir took the Slayer’s Oath after failing to protect his kin during a Skaven incursion into the lower mines. Since that day, he has sought redemption through battle, carving a path of destruction through the enemies of Karak Izor. Clad in nothing but his tattoos and a rune-etched greataxe, Hugnir’s presence is a terrifying sight to behold. His axe glows with a baleful light, its runes flaring with deadly power as they bite into daemonic flesh. Though he has forsaken all claim to leadership, Hugnir’s deeds inspire both awe and dread among his kin. He stands as a living reminder of the price of failure, and of the unyielding strength of Dwarfen resolve. Many whisper that Hugnir’s final battle shall be one for the ages, a clash that will see him redeemed in the eyes of the Ancestors, or lost forever to the annals of history as a legend without equal.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_izor_first_5}Drakk Gunmarsson is the stalwart guardian of Karak Izor’s western territories, a region often threatened by Greenskin raiders and marauding Beastmen. His thick, craggy brow gives him a perpetually stern look, and his braided auburn beard is streaked with soot from countless battles fought in defence of the hold. Drakk is a born warrior, clad in rune-inscribed gromril plate that has withstood the blows of trolls and the claws of Chaos beasts alike. His weapon of choice is a colossal rune-axe that hums with runes of cleaving and thunder, capable of rending even the hardiest foe in twain. Renowned for his mastery of defensive warfare, Drakk has time and again turned narrow mountain passes into slaughterfields for invading armies. Though gruff and taciturn, his loyalty to King Kazran and his love for Karak Izor are beyond reproach. To Drakk, the hold’s walls are sacred, and he will fight to his last breath to ensure they are never breached.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_izor_first_6}Gorrik Flintshield is the indomitable Captain of Karak Izor’s elite shieldwall regiment. His name is spoken with reverence by the warriors under his command and with dread by the Greenskins who have faced him in battle. Gorrik’s stout frame is encased in gromril plate, and his shield is a massive slab of rune-inscribed steel, said to have turned aside the crushing blow of a Wyvern’s tail. His weapon of choice is a hefty warhammer, forged to deliver devastating strikes that shatter both armour and bone. A veteran of countless engagements, Gorrik is famed for his unyielding resolve and tactical acumen. He has held narrow mountain passes against overwhelming odds, his shieldwall standing firm as the mountains themselves. His leadership is direct and uncompromising, demanding discipline and valour from his warriors. Yet, his loyalty to his kin and his hold is absolute. Off the battlefield, Gorrik is a staunch traditionalist, deeply devoted to the ancestors and the preservation of Dwarfen customs. He frequently confers with King Kazran Grimbrow on matters of defence and military strategy, ensuring that Karak Izor remains an impenetrable bastion against the foes that try to assail it.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_izor_first_7}Barik Stonehelm is the master of Karak Izor’s Forgeworks, a labyrinthine complex of anvils, workshops, and roaring furnaces where the hold’s most formidable war machines and firearms are wrought. His thick black beard is singed at the edges, and his hands are perpetually stained with soot and oil, a testament to a lifetime of toil amidst flame and steel. Barik’s armour is a patchwork of riveted steel plates and reinforced leather, festooned with tools, cogs, and mechanisms. His famed mechanical gauntlet, powered by concealed gears and counterweights, is a marvel of his own invention. He wields a masterfully engineered handgun that fires explosive rounds, and he carries an assortment of grenades and experimental devices, each capable of altering the course of battle in an instant. His ingenuity has earned him the grudging respect of even the most conservative Runelords, and his creations, from flame-belching cannons to armoured gyrocopters, stand at the forefront of Karak Izor’s defences. Though gruff and often irascible, Barik is fiercely protective of both his kin and his craft. He insists on testing his inventions personally, and has been known to lead his fellow engineers into battle to ensure their machines perform to exacting standards. Barik’s relentless innovation and battlefield prowess have secured his place in the annals of Karak Izor’s history as one of its most gifted and unorthodox minds.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_izor_first_8}Thorik Stonebrow is the Keeper of the Oathstone, a sacred relic of Karak Izor that symbolises the unbreakable vows of its people. A towering figure among his kin, Thorik’s beard is streaked with grey, and his craggy features bear the weight of centuries of unflinching duty. His armour, adorned with the runes of the ancestors, gleams with a dull, battle-worn sheen, and his warhammer is a fearsome relic said to shatter the resolve of even the most steadfast foes. Thorik’s role as Keeper is both ceremonial and martial. He presides over the swearing of oaths, ensuring that promises made to the hold and its king are neither spoken lightly nor forgotten. In battle, he is a resolute presence, often standing at the heart of the shieldwall, his voice a booming reminder of the vows his warriors have sworn. Honourable and unyielding, Thorik is driven by a deep-rooted sense of duty. He is known to hold grudges with an iron grip, pursuing retribution for any slight against his hold or his kin with relentless resolve. Though his demeanour is stern and uncompromising, Thorik is deeply respected by his peers. His unwavering devotion to Karak Izor and its ancient traditions embodies the very essence of Dwarven resilience.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_izor_first_9}Skorri Ironvein is the indomitable commander of Karak Izor’s elite warriors, tasked with patrolling the lower tunnels and mines of the hold. His broad frame and weathered visage speak of a lifetime spent beneath the mountain, where danger lurks in every shadow. Skorri’s armour is a masterwork of function and craftsmanship, reinforced with thick gromril plates and etched with runes of endurance, built to withstand the crushing blows of subterranean foes. His axe, perfectly balanced for the tight confines of the tunnels, has claimed countless Greenskin and Skaven lives. Skorri’s leadership is defined by pragmatism and adaptability. He knows the labyrinthine depths of Karak Izor as others know the lines of their own hands, able to read the stone like a map. His warriors trust him implicitly, knowing his calm demeanour and sharp instincts have saved them from ambushes and cave-ins more times than they can recall. Off duty, Skorri is a private and contemplative figure, often found in the lower halls inspecting the mines or sharpening his axe. Though he rarely partakes in the revelries of the upper halls, his loyalty to Karak Izor is beyond question, and his name is spoken with reverence among those who brave the dark depths.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_izor_first_10}Borri Gembeard is the Master Prospector of Karak Izor, a title of great prestige in a hold famed for its abundance of precious metals and gemstones. His braided beard glitters with embedded jewels, each one a testament to his unmatched skill in uncovering the mountain’s hidden wealth. His pickaxe serves both as a tool and a weapon, its haft inlaid with silver runes of precision and strength, while his armour gleams with polished copper and gold plates, reflecting the riches he has brought forth. Borri is a Dwarf of boundless curiosity and relentless determination. He has led countless expeditions into uncharted tunnels, his keen eye and deep knowledge of geology uncovering rich veins of ore and gemstone that have greatly enriched the hold. Though not a frontline warrior, Borri is no stranger to combat, having defended his prospecting parties against Skaven raiders and the many beasts that dwell in the deep places of the world. In the council chambers, Borri’s counsel is highly valued; his insights into the mountain’s resources are key to Karak Izor’s economic strength and strategic planning. Despite his wealth and renown, he remains grounded, often found in the common halls recounting tales of peril and discovery over a well-earned tankard of ale. To his kin, Borri Gembeard represents the enduring bond between the Dwarfs and the mountains they call home, a living symbol of resilience, industry, and ancestral pride.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kaferkammaz_factionleader}King Skalf Redbeard is a ruler caught between tradition and diplomacy, a stout and battle-hardened Dwarf whose rule has seen both prosperity and strife. Clad in masterfully forged gromril plate and bearing the axe, Oathkeeper, a relic of his line. Skalf stands as a beacon of stubborn resilience and pragmatic wisdom. His namesake beard, once the fiery red of a forge’s heart, has begun to grey with age. Centuries ago, King Skalf did what few Dwarf rulers would dare, he brokered trade agreements with the Wood Elves of Athel Loren. While many of his kin scowled at the notion of dealing with the fickle Asrai, Skalf saw opportunity. Timber from the Elves strengthened the hold’s construction efforts, while Dwarfen steel and crafted wares found their way into Elven hands. The accords brought wealth and stability to Karak Kaferkammaz, and for a time, both races benefited from a rare peace in the Vaults. But the years have not been kind to these ties. Old grudges and shifting alliances have strained the fragile peace. The Asrai grow ever more secretive and untrusting, while Dwarfs of the hold grumble that their generosity has been met with aloof disdain. Skalf, for all his efforts, walks a narrow path, striving to uphold the accords lest both sides descend into open war. He is wise enough to know that a single wrong word, broken promise, or bloodied axe could undo centuries of uneasy cooperation. Yet, should the Elves betray their trust, should they draw first blood, then Skalf Redbeard will not hesitate. The oaths of peace will be cast into the forge, and Karak Kaferkammaz shall march to war. Until that day comes, the King stands firm, balancing the legacy of his rule upon the edge of a finely honed axe.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kaferkammaz_first_2}Born beneath the vaulted halls of Karak Kaferkammaz, Prince Elmador Skalfsson was raised in the shadow of his father, King Skalf Redbeard, a ruler known for his diplomacy and pragmatism. But where his father saw opportunity, Elmador saw compromise, and where Skalf sought peace, Elmador seethed with resentment. He was a child of war, raised on the stories of Elven treachery and the endless struggles against the beastmen and raiders of the underway. To him, the treaties with the Wood Elves were not a mark of wisdom, but a stain upon Dwarfen honour. Clad in finely crafted gromril armour, adorned with the rune-etched pauldrons of Clan Skalfsson, Elmador is every inch the warrior-prince. His warhammer was forged in defiance of the Asrai, a symbol of his belief that Dwarfs should not barter with those who live by deception and magic. He leads patrols into the northern reaches of the hold, watching the tree line with suspicion, ever wary of an Elven knife in the dark. To his credit, Elmador does not defy his father openly. He is a Dwarf of discipline and respect, and his loyalty to King Skalf remains unquestioned. But deep within, he waits for the day when he will take the throne, when he can right the wrongs of the past and cast aside the treaties his father signed. The Wood Elves, in his mind, are fickle and faithless, and he believes that sooner or later, they will turn on the Dwarfs as they always have. While others hope for continued peace, Elmador prepares for war. He strengthens the hold’s defences, gathers warriors to his banner, and ensures that should the Elves so much as step beyond their borders, Karak Kaferkammaz will be ready. He is a hammer waiting to fall, and when it does, the echoes of his wrath may shake the Vaults themselves.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kaferkammaz_first_3}Once a proud and decorated thane of Karak Kaferkammaz, Kazran Firebrand was a name spoken with both reverence and sorrow. He had stood as a shield for his kin, his axe breaking many foes upon the bloodied stone of the underway. His greatest failure came when the hold was beset by a monstrous daemon of Tzeentch, a creature of ever-shifting flesh and sorcery that twisted reality itself. Kazran led the charge against it, his warriors fighting with unyielding Dwarfen might, but in the end, the beast was vanquished only at a terrible cost. His own brother, Durn, fell to its sorcery, his body turning to lifeless crystal before Kazran ’s very eyes. Wracked with grief and bound by the burden of shame, Kazran did what many before him had done, he cast aside his name, his wealth, and his place within the hold, taking up the oath of the Slayer. Yet his path was not of blind fury; he sought vengeance upon daemons and every other vile thing that crawled from the depths of Chaos. He fights wherever the taint of the Dark Gods is found, his great axe runed and reforged with burning glyphs, turning the flesh of daemons to ash with each strike. His once-proud golden hair is now a wild mane of fire, bound in the ancient oath-locks of Grimnir, his body adorned with scars both physical and spiritual. Though his name is still whispered with respect in Karak Kaferkammaz, he has no home, no clan, no kin, only the path to atonement, and the promise of one day meeting his doom in battle.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kaferkammaz_first_4}The forges of Karak Kaferkammaz burn hot under the watchful gaze of Runelord Grumli Runesoul, one of the most respected and formidable runesmiths of the Vaults. To him, runes are not mere tools, but the sacred words of the Ancestor Gods, the very essence of Dwarfen might and endurance. In the face of war, it is his duty to bind steel with the strength of the mountain, and to ensure that the warriors of Karak Kaferkammaz go into battle clad in gromril-wrought protection, infused with the oldest magics of the Dawi. Unlike many of his peers who remain within their forges, Grumli is known to take to the field of battle, standing amidst the shieldwalls of his kin, chanting oaths of defiance as he strikes his rune-covered hammer against the earth. The very ground beneath the Dwarfs becomes as unyielding as iron, their weapons glow with runic might, and spells hurled by enemy wizards break like waves upon rock. A grim and taciturn figure, Grumli bears a deep distrust of outsiders, particularly the Wood Elves, whom he believes toy too freely with the forces of magic. He opposed the treaties of King Skalf Redbeard, arguing that Elven trickery could never be trusted, and to this day, he ensures that should the accords ever break, the warriors of Karak Kaferkammaz will be ready. His personal warhammer is a relic of the past, a weapon that once sealed the gates of the hold against an endless horde of beastmen. Now, it is wielded to break the foes of the Dawi, and to remind all who stand before him that Dwarfs are not ruled by words, but by steel, stone, and the wisdom of the Ancestors.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kaferkammaz_first_5}The underpasses and deep roads of Karak Kaferkammaz are as perilous as the wilds above, filled with the skittering menace of the Skaven, the bestial hordes of the Beastmen, and the ever-present threat of Greenskin warbands. Yet for every ambush, every attempted invasion, there stands a wall of steel and resolve in the form of Lord Borri Ironfist, Shieldmaster of the Underway, and the unyielding defender of the deep roads. Borri is a Dwarf of iron discipline, a warrior who has spent centuries battling the filth of the underground, ensuring that the lifeblood of the hold, the mines and trade routes, remains secure. He has fought in battles where the torches barely glowed, where the enemy came in tides without number, and where the only thing that held the line was the unshakable will of Dawi warriors standing shoulder to shoulder. Clad in blackened gromril plate, his shield adorned with the sigil of Karak Kaferkammaz, Borri is a warrior of unyielding endurance, a rock amidst the storm. He wields a weapon once thought lost in the depths of a collapsed tunnel, recovered only after Borri personally led an expedition into the darkest reaches of the underway to reclaim it from the skeletal remains of a long-dead Thane.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kaferkammaz_first_6}Beneath the towering peaks and sturdy walls of Karak Kaferkammaz lies a vast network of tunnels and mines that produce the ores and precious stones in the Vaults. Overseeing these treacherous depths is Lord Ulfar Stonevein, a seasoned miner turned leader, whose unmatched knowledge of the underway makes him vital to the hold’s prosperity and safety. Ulfar began his life as many Dwarfs do, with pickaxe and lantern, carving out his legacy with stone-dusted hands and sweat. It was his instinct for finding rich veins of ore and his iron resolve in defending his crews from the horrors of the deep that earned him both renown and his title. When Skaven burrowed into the lower mines, it was Ulfar who led the counterattack, wielding his twin axes with a fury that sent the ratmen scurrying back into the darkness. Though his scarred face and grizzled beard mark his years of hardship, his eyes still gleam with the hunger for discovery. His loyalty to Karak Kaferkammaz is as solid as the mountains, and he’s known to clash with more cautious lords, pushing for deeper excavations and greater risk. Yet those who follow him know that Ulfar leads from the front, where the rock is hardest and danger is greatest, he stands with his kin.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kaferkammaz_first_7}When the horns of war sound through the hold, it is Lord Hargin Emberfist who answers first, marching at the head of the Iron Guard, the elite warriors sworn to defend Karak Kaferkammaz. Known for his fiery temper and indomitable strength, Hargin has spent centuries on the battlefield, earning his name when his gauntleted fist crushed the skull of a beastman champion during a desperate last stand at Stormcleft Pass. Clad in rune-inscribed gromril armor, Hargin wields an ancient warhammer said to contain the wrath of the mountains themselves. His booming voice carries commands like thunder, and his presence on the battlefield inspires Dwarfs to stand firm, no matter how dire the odds. He has fought against Skaven hordes, Greenskin raiders, and twisting Chaos monstrosities, never retreating, never surrendering.Despite his martial prowess, Hargin is no mere brute—he is a keen tactician, respected advisor, and staunch traditionalist. He believes that the treaties with the Wood Elves have softened the hold, and frequently clashes with King Skalf Redbeard, urging a return to Dwarfen self-reliance and strength.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kaferkammaz_first_8}In times of war and peace alike, it is the strength of the home that sustains the Dawi, and Lord Brokk Stonemantle ensures that Karak Kaferkammaz’s heart remains strong. As Keeper of the Hearth and Hold, Brokk oversees the craftsmen’s guilds, the armories, and the great halls, ensuring that tradition and prosperity endure even when the world beyond the gates grows dark. Brokk’s broad shoulders and granite-like demeanor mirror the very stones of the hold itself. His beard, thick and silver, is braided with rings of honor, each marking a victory of industry and diplomacy. He is no mere frontline warrior, his greatest battles lie in council chambers and trade halls, where he negotiates with shrewd cunning and ensures the hold’s wealth flows steadily. Despite his diplomatic nature, Brokk is no friend of the Wood Elves. He remembers every slight and broken promise, and while he respects King Skalf’s efforts for peace, he trusts steel and gold far more than elven words. Yet Brokk’s calm wisdom and strategic mind make him a valued advisor.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kaferkammaz_first_9}Wherever Karak Kaferkammaz’s warriors stand their ground, Lord Kargun Stoneheart is at the forefront, an immovable wall of steel and stone. Known for his implacable nature and unshakable resolve, Kargun has become a living embodiment of Dwarfen endurance. His face, weathered and scarred, bears the marks of countless battles, and his eyes burn with the fierce light of a warrior who has never known defeat. Kargun’s name was earned in the defence of the hold’s outer tunnels, where he held a collapsing line against a tide of Beastmen for three days without rest. It is said that even when his shield arm was broken and his axe dulled, he fought on, standing amidst the bodies of the fallen until reinforcements arrived. His armour, a fortress of overlapping gromril plates, bears the scars of a thousand battles, and his shield has turned aside blows that would have felled a giant. Despite his grim and often silent demeanour, Kargun inspires fierce loyalty among his warriors. They know that where he stands, no foe will break through, and no ground will be lost. While he respects King Skalf’s efforts for diplomacy, Kargun believes peace can only be preserved through strength, and that every treaty must be backed by the might of Dwarfen steel.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_kaferkammaz_first_10}Lord Hugnir Stoutshield, Guardian of the Outer Gates. As the Warden of the Outer Gates, Hugnir’s duty lies in defending the entrance to the hold itself, standing against the tide of invaders that constantly threaten the Dawi’s home. From Greenskin warbands to Beastmen raiders, Hugnir has faced them all and turned them back with unwavering resolve. A broad and imposing figure, Hugnir ’s presence on the battlefield is as immovable as the stone he defends. His gromril shield is a legendary artifact said to have withstood the hammer blows of an Orc Warlord and the sorcerous fire of a Bray-Shaman without yielding. His axe has split the skulls of countless foes and remains a symbol of his dedication to Karak Kaferkammaz. Despite his gruff demeanor and battle-hardened exterior, Hugnir is deeply loyal to King Skalf Redbeard. He has voiced his concerns about the strained relations with the Wood Elves but remains steadfast in his belief that the unity and strength of the hold come first. He views Prince Elmador’s hatred of the Asrai with caution, fearing the rashness that could lead to unnecessary conflict.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_norn_factionleader}The Grey Mountains are an unforgiving land, their stone poor in ore and their slopes devoid of the riches that fuel the great holds of the World's Edge Mountains. And yet, Karak Norn endures, not through wealth, but through the unyielding will of its king, Brokk Ironpick. A Dwarf as hard and unrelenting as the mountains themselves, King Brokk has ruled over Karak Norn for centuries with the same iron resolve that first drove his ancestors to carve their hold from barren stone. Brokk Ironpick is a figure of grim determination. His face, lined and weathered like the cliffs of his homeland, speaks of a life spent battling both enemies and despair. His long, steel-grey beard is plaited with iron rings, and his eyes, dark and unwavering, carry the weight of every hardship his people have endured. Clad in heavy gromril armour etched with the ancient runes of endurance and fortitude, Brokk stands as a living symbol of his hold’s resilience. In battle, King Brokk is a force to behold. He wields an ancient and revered weapon, passed down through generations, a massive pickaxe forged from blackened gromril, its head covered in runes of shattering and spite. Though unconventional for a king, the weapon embodies the unyielding perseverance of Karak Norn’s people, as well as their relentless drive to extract whatever meagre wealth their mountains might still hide. Despite his dour nature, Brokk is a king deeply respected, if not beloved, by his subjects. He demands much from his people, pushing them to dig deeper, fight harder, and endure longer than they ever thought possible. Yet he also shoulders those burdens himself, leading from the front in both war and labour. It is not uncommon to find the king in the mines alongside his kin, his iron pick striking stone with the same tireless rhythm that drives his every action. Brokk’s relationship with the neighbouring realms is one of careful pragmatism. He maintains uneasy truces with the Wood Elves of Athel Loren, though his mistrust of the Asrai runs deep. The Bretonnians, with their pretensions of chivalry and their incessant squabbling, earn little more than his scorn, though he will trade with them when it serves Karak Norn’s interests. With the Empire, there is respect, if not warmth, Brokk values their industry and discipline, but remains ever watchful for signs of human folly. As the years wear on and the mountain’s riches continue to dwindle, the weight upon Brokk Ironpick’s shoulders grows heavier. Yet still he stands, unyielding and defiant.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_norn_first_2}Few names in Karak Norn inspire sorrow like that of Thingrim Stonefury. Once a proud Thane of his clan, Thingrim was a warrior of steadfast honour and uncompromising loyalty, until the day his hold suffered a grievous attack from the twisted forces of Chaos. In the defense of his kin, Thingrim’s only son fell to the claws of a monstrous Daemon, and with his death, something inside Thingrim broke. Consumed by grief and the need for vengeance, he shaved his head, dyed his beard in the fiery hues of shame and wrath, and took the Slayer’s oath. It's been many years since then. Thingrim , now a Daemonslayer, is a tempest of fury on the battlefield. His Runic Greataxe, Runebranded relic of his clan, strikes with the strength of an avalanche and the speed of a lightning storm. The scars that crisscross his hardened frame tell stories of battles that would have slain lesser Dwarfs, but Thingrim fights on, seeking the death he believes his failures have earned. Yet despite his oath, fate has denied him that end. Whether he stands against the Beastmen of the Grey Mountains or the raiding warbands of Greenskins, he emerges bloodied but unbroken, his defiance a symbol of Karak Norn’s unyielding spirit. Though his presence brings unease,reminders of oaths broken and burdens borne. Thingrim Stonefury remains one of Karak Norn’s greatest champions, his axe carving out legends even as he seeks his doom.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_norn_first_3}In the cold, mineral-poor depths of Karak Norn, the runes burn brightest. Hakon is the master of Runecraft, his anvil a place of solemn power and his forge a sanctuary of incandescent heat. As the spiritual and magical guardian of the hold, Hakon wields the wisdom of centuries and the strength of enchanted steel. Clad in rune-etched gromril and bearing an ancient Runehammer, Hakon Emberforge is a vision of Dawi tradition and power. The air around him hums with the presence of binding runes and ancient protections, and his every strike on the battlefield leaves searing marks of warding and destruction. He is known for his stoic demeanor and his fierce dedication to the hold’s safety, channeling his craft into armaments that withstand the ravages of war and enchantments that ward against the corruption of Chaos. Despite his isolation in the forge, Hakon is no stranger to battle. When the need arises, he marches with the armies of Karak Norn, his presence bolstering the warriors around him and his runes turning aside the deadliest of blows. He has stood at King Brokk Ironpick’s side on countless campaigns, his magic tempering the iron resolve of the hold with fire and stone.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_norn_first_4}Deep beneath Karak Norn lies a maze of old tunnels and sealed vaults, remnants from when the Grey Mountains were thought to hold vast riches. Most have been abandoned to time and shadow, but certain vaults still flicker with torchlight. This is where Mardin Grum, known as Iron-Eye, Marches. A master of subterranean warfare and an obsessive preserver of lost history, Mardin has made it his life’s work to explore, reclaim, and restore the lower levels of the hold. His nickname comes from the heavy iron visor he wears over his eyes, a contraption of mirrored lenses and runic etchings said to help him see the traces of magical taint, structural weakness, or buried secrets. Mardin's warriors are hardened tunnel-fighters, trained to combat beasts of the dark and collapse-prone ruins. While Mardin rarely ventures topside, when he does, his voice is heavy with knowledge of things best left forgotten and dangers long entombed.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_norn_first_5}Among the lords of Karak Norn, Dorrik stands as the embodiment of the Dawi’s most sacred tradition: the keeping and settling of grudges. As the appointed Grudgekeeper of the hold, it is Dorrik’s solemn duty to maintain the Great Book of Grudges, a task he executes with unwavering diligence and an ironclad sense of justice. With every slight against the Dawi recorded, Dorrik fights not just for victory, but for retribution, his hammer striking with the weight of millennia of unforgiven insults and unavenged deaths. Despite his grim duties, Dorrik is known for his steady hand and even temper. He advises King Brokk Ironpick with wisdom honed by decades of experience, balancing the fires of vengeance with the need for diplomacy and patience. Yet when the time comes for reckoning, none are as fierce or relentless in battle, and every foe who falls to his hammer is one step closer to settling the ancient debts of Karak Norn. In times of peace, Dorrik is the voice of caution and resolve. In times of war, he is the storm that rights every wrong. And through it all, he remains the living memory of his people’s trials, and the iron promise that no insult shall go unanswered.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_norn_first_6}Among the grim and stubborn Dwarfs of Karak Norn, few are more driven, or more quietly desperate, than Lord Varnik Hammerdeep. A direct descendant of one of the founding prospectors who settled the Grey Mountains on whispers of wealth, Varnik bears the burden of generations of unfulfilled promises. With pick and lantern in hand, he leads the Miners of Karak Norn, tirelessly scouring the unstable bedrock for the motherlode his ancestors believed in so fervently. Varnik’s halls are lined not with treasure, but with maps, layer upon layer of meticulously charted shafts, dead ends, and dangerous collapses. His armour is dulled by dust and time, his beard singed more than once by underground gas pockets, and his face is a canvas of soot and iron-hard resolve. The younger Dwarfs see him as a relic clinging to myth, but the older Dawi respect him deeply, for he does not just seek gold, but vindication. Varnik will either strike true and restore the pride of Karak Norn, or he will die in the dark, pick in hand.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_norn_first_7}A philosopher-lord in a hold starving for fortune, Kazrik Grimtone is as much scholar as warrior. He is the Keeper of the Stone Choir, a subterranean chamber of old oathstones, rune-inscribed memorials, and ancestral records preserved from fallen holds like Mount Silverspear. Though not a Runelord himself, he guards the histories with fierce pride and is one of the few who can recite ancient lineages from memory. Kazrik rarely takes the field unless provoked, but when he does, it is with a grim fury born of duty to memory and blood. His axe was forged from the smelted remnants of his ancestral hearth and hums with a deep, echoing resonance when swung. Dour and severe, Kazrik resents the Wood Elves most of all, not for war, but for their perceived arrogance, their indifference to the past. He dreams not of conquest or gold, but of a time when the Dwarfs of the Grey Mountains are no longer seen as relics clinging to stories, but as a people once more feared and respected.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_norn_first_8}Though Karak Norn is now his home, Dengeir Flintmantle was born in exile, beneath the shattered remnants of Mount Silverspear. He was just a beardling when the hold fell to the onslaught of Greenskins, yet the memory of fire and stone, of screaming kin and shattered oaths, burns within him like a forge with no rest. Now one of Karak Norn’s senior lords, Dengeir has sworn that the legacy of Silverspear shall not fade into dust. A master tactician and field commander, Dengeir leads an elite formation of warriors descended from Mount Silverspear. Their armor bears soot-markings to remind them of their ruined home, and their axes are tempered with bitter memories. Dengeir himself wears a heavy steel mantle, scorched and fused with volcanic glass, taken from the heartforge of Silverspear during its last days. He is known for his cutting insight and his scathing words, even among his own kin, but in battle he is a roaring firestorm of wrath and discipline. While others search the Grey Mountains for riches, Dengeir searches for vengeance.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_norn_first_9}Lord Dori Yngvarsson commands the southern sentry halls of Montdidier Pass, one of the most heavily fortified gateways in the Grey Mountains. A veteran of countless skirmishes and tense stand-offs with Bretonnian knights and wandering warbands, Dori is the embodiment of Dwarfen vigilance. Shorter than most, and built more like a stone block than a warrior, he is slow to speak and slower still to trust. He maintains the walls and bolt thrower nests of the pass with obsessive care, and while others in Karak Norn grumble about dwindling prospects, Dori prepares. “Peace is but the whetstone of war,” he says, often to his weary engineers. With a small but elite garrison, he oversees the southern reaches of Karak Norn’s domain and is often the first to raise the alarm of approaching trouble. Though little known outside the hold, his name is spoken with quiet reverence among his sentries, for few have held the line so long, and with such unflinching resolve.

{=str_encyclopedia_tor_dw_lord_karak_norn_first_10}In the shadowed depths of Karak Norn lies a chamber known as the Weeping Vault, named for the slow, eternal drip of mineral-laden water from the cracked ceiling, a sound that echoes like a funeral dirge. It is here that Lord Bardek Stonesong holds watch, not over wealth or weapons, but over memory itself. For the Weeping Vault serves as the final resting place of countless Dwarfs whose bodies were never recovered, miners lost to collapse, warriors fallen in far-off battles, clans who vanished in the dark, all chasing after their ancestor’s hopes and dreams of wealth in the depths. Bardek, once a master stonemason and tomb-carver, was chosen to tend the Vault after a cave-in claimed his two brothers and dozens of his kin. In mourning, he took up the mantle not of vengeance, but of remembrance. His great mantle is fashioned from dark stone-weave, etched with runes of endurance and names of the fallen, worn over armor that bears more weight in grief than in steel. He carries no shield, only a greataxe, whose edge sings when it strikes, a haunting tone like keening granite.
